sub_feature: Date-range Segmented — state desync on browser nav

recommendation: Make the header a button only over the title row (or a disclosure-triangle button) and move the body+action buttons OUTSIDE the header button, or convert to a real <details>/Radix Collapsible with the trigger as the only interactive element in the header. target_gap: No action-row overflow/clip at 360px in compact/table views.
evidence: Compact variant renders actions in a trailing 'flex shrink-0 items-center gap-1.5' cluster. On the patterns source that's FOUR buttons (Confirm/Address/Resolve/Dismiss) and even insights have THREE; with shrink-0 + a title beside them on a 360px viewport the cluster cannot wrap and will overflow / clip in table view and grouped-compact rows.
recommendation: Allow the compact action cluster to collapse to an overflow menu (kebab) on narrow viewports, or drop to the lowest-priority actions inline + a 'More' menu. Don't keep 4 shrink-0 buttons next to the title on mobile.

sub_feature: KPI tile group / grouping landmark semantics
target_gap: Labelled grouping for the KPI band and grouping control.
evidence: The 3-up MetricCard grid has no group label/region, and the 'Group' Segmented control sits in a bare flex row; the metric tiles read as three disconnected figures to AT. The grouped sections do use aria-labelledby (good), but the summary band and the group-by control lack a labelled grouping/region.
recommendation: Wrap the KPI tiles in a labelled region (e.g. role=group aria-label='Signal summary') and ensure the group-by Segmented has its label associated; minor but it raises the surface to the a11y polish bar.

target_gap: Every interactive control must be fully keyboard operable (WCAG 2.1.1). The card's primary 'open detail' affordance is mouse-only today.
evidence: const interactiveProps = interactive ? { tabIndex: 0, role: 'button' as const } : {}; — the card renders <article role="button" tabIndex=0 onClick={() => setOpenRowId(row.id)}> but there is NO onKeyDown/onKeyUp handler anywhere in InsightCard (grep confirms none). A native <article> with role=button does not fire onClick on Enter/Space.
recommendation: Add an onKeyDown handler that calls the click handler on Enter and Space (and preventDefault on Space), or render the interactive surface as a real <button>/wrap the title in a <button>. Ensure the focusable element exposes an accessible name.

sub_feature: Pattern card — action buttons vs card click target
target_gap: No nested interactive controls; each control performs exactly one action. Today the row's click target and its buttons collide.
evidence: InsightCard is rendered with interactive + onClick={() => setOpenRowId(row.id)} (role="button"), and its `actions` slot contains real <Button> elements (Confirm/Address/Resolve/Dismiss) whose onClick handlers (handleConfirmPattern etc.) never call e.stopPropagation(). Result: a <button> nested inside a role=button article (ARIA 4.1.2 nested-interactive violation) AND clicking 'Resolve' both resolves the pattern and bubbles up to open the detail sheet.
recommendation: Do not make the whole card role=button while it also hosts action buttons. Either (a) make only a non-action region (overline/title) the open-detail trigger, or (b) stopPropagation in each action handler and drop role=button from the article when actions are present. Resolve the nested-interactive violation.

sub_feature: Confirm / Address / Resolve / Dismiss — pending + double-submit guard
target_gap: Layer 3 requires guarded, visibly-pending mutations; today actions are fire-and-forget with no in-flight affordance.
evidence: const [, startActionTransition] = useTransition(); — the isPending boolean is discarded. All four pattern lifecycle handlers run inside startActionTransition but no button receives busy/disabled. A coach can click 'Resolve' twice before the optimistic removal lands, firing resolvePattern twice.
recommendation: Capture isPending from useTransition (or a per-row in-flight Set) and set busy/disabled on the row's action buttons while the mutation is in flight; the Fairway Button already supports busy with a spinner + aria-busy.

sub_feature: Per-row pattern action feedback (visibility of system status / undo)
target_gap: Layer 3 requires immediate visible feedback + undo on consequential actions; pattern triage gives neither.
evidence: setNotice (the success InlineNotice) is ONLY called inside runBulk (insights-only). handleAddressPattern/handleResolvePattern/handleDismissPattern optimistically remove the row (removePatternOptimistic) with no toast and no undo; handleConfirmPattern flips the row silently. A coach who taps 'Resolve' sees the pattern vanish with zero confirmation and no way to undo.
recommendation: Emit a success notice/toast on each per-row pattern action (e.g. "Pattern resolved") and offer an Undo that restores lifecycle_state (the optimistic snapshot `prev` is already captured and could power it). Honors Nielsen #1 (status) and #3 (control & freedom).

sub_feature: Validate pattern — notes / severity / create-focus-area (sub-feature completeness)
target_gap: Layer 3 requires implied sub-features to exist; the validate workflow's notes/focus-area/severity are implemented server-side but dead in the UI.
evidence: handleConfirmPattern calls validatePattern(p.id, { isAccurate: true, severity: p.severity }) — it hard-codes severity to the DB column (which is 'medium' for ~all rows) and never passes `notes` or `createFocusArea`. The action (pattern-management.ts validatePattern lines 464-499) supports coach notes (resolution_notes), an explicit severity, and createFocusAreaFromPatternInternal, but none of that is reachable from the live UI.
recommendation: Surface a confirm affordance that lets the coach (optionally) set severity, add a note, and check 'create a focus area' — wiring the existing validatePattern parameters. At minimum pass the DERIVED priority instead of the always-'medium' p.severity so confirmation doesn't write a misleading severity.

target_gap: C4 'Tables' + match-to-real-world: a control labeled Table must produce a table or not claim to.
evidence: VIEW_OPTIONS includes { value: 'table', label: 'Table' }, but the table branch renders `rows.map((r) => renderCard(r, { compact: true }))` — a flat list of compact cards. There is no <table>, no sticky header, no columns, no consistent row grid, no multi-select.
recommendation: Either implement a real table (sticky header, column headers, aligned cells, row hover, the criterion C4 contract) or rename the option to something honest like 'Compact'/'List'.

sub_feature: Group control — no-op in Table view
target_gap: Every control must have an effect in the state it is shown; the Group toggle is inert in Table view.
evidence: grouped = !smartDefaultActive && (view === 'grouped' || (view === 'feed' && groupBy !== 'none')); — so in view==='table' `grouped` is always false. Yet the Group segmented control (By player / By category / Flat) is still rendered whenever `!loading && rows.length>0 && !smartDefaultActive`, including Table view, where changing groupBy has zero visible effect.
recommendation: Hide the Group control in Table view (it only applies to feed/grouped), or make Table honor groupBy. A control that visibly does nothing fails Nielsen consistency + the no-dead-UI gate.

sub_feature: Selection / bulk-action chrome exposed but unreachable for patterns
target_gap: Sub-feature completeness: insights get bulk + multi-select; patterns silently get none despite the same toolbar.
evidence: The SignalsToolbar is wired with selectedCount={selectedIds.size}/onClearSelection and the Toolbar reserves a whole bulk-action bar slot, but on patterns bulkActions is undefined (bulkActions = !isPatterns ? (...) : undefined) and NO pattern card ever exposes a checkbox to populate selectedIds. So patterns can never enter selection mode — a bulk capability that visibly exists in the shared toolbar contract is dead on this surface.
recommendation: Either add per-row selection + a patterns bulk-action set (e.g. bulk dismiss/address), or document/inert the selection contract for patterns so the workspace isn't carrying invisible dead bulk chrome. Patterns triage across a roster is exactly where bulk would help.

sub_feature: Mobile — compact-card trailing action cluster (4 buttons)
target_gap: Mobile parity: the default patterns layout risks horizontal overflow / title crush with its 4-button row.
evidence:
In compact/grouped (the patterns DEFAULT view, groupBy='player'), actions render in a non-wrapping trailing cluster: `
{actions}
`. For patterns that cluster is FOUR buttons (Confirm, Address, Resolve, Dismiss) with no responsive collapse; on a narrow viewport this either overflows the row or squeezes the title (which is `line-clamp-1` + `min-w-0`).
recommendation: Collapse the secondary pattern actions (Address/Resolve/Dismiss) into an overflow menu on small screens, or allow the action cluster to wrap below the title in compact view, keeping >=44px touch targets.

sub_feature: Detail panel (InsightPanel sheet) — pattern action set vs card action set inconsistency
target_gap: Consistency: scanned vs read views of the same pattern must offer the same lifecycle actions.
evidence: The card row exposes Confirm + Address + Resolve + Dismiss, but the opened InsightPanel (panelActions for patterns) exposes only Address / Confirm / Dismiss — Resolve is missing, and the labels/order differ from the card. The same signal therefore offers a different action set scanned vs read.
recommendation: Make the panel's pattern action set match the card's (include Resolve; align labels/order) so a coach has consistent options whether scanning or reading. Nielsen #4 consistency.

sub_feature: Legacy ErrorState styling leaks (flag-OFF fork, but ships token violations)
target_gap: Token discipline (C2) — raw red-* and text-white literals; only relevant if the legacy fork remains shippable.
evidence: ErrorState uses raw color literals not on the Fairway tone scale: bg-red-100, text-red-500, from-red-500/5, plus text-white on bg-primary-600. This is the flag-OFF branch (out of strict grade scope) but it is still in the patterns page file and would render if isRedesignEnabled() were false; the live fork uses an honest InlineNotice instead.
recommendation: If the legacy fork is being retired, delete this ErrorState; otherwise migrate it to fw-danger / surface tokens for brand consistency. (Noted for completeness — live path uses InlineNotice and is fine.)

sub_feature: Patterns header KPI row — no deltas/trends (dashboard structure)
target_gap: C3 dashboard structure: KPI tiles should carry delta+trend, not bare counts, to read as premium.
evidence: The 3 MetricCards (Open signals / Urgent+high / Loaded) render value-only — no delta chip, no sparkline, no trend, despite MetricCard fully supporting delta/sparkline. 'Loaded' is honest but is a thin KPI band for a premium triage workspace.
recommendation: Where honest data exists (e.g. week-over-week new patterns, resolved-this-week), add a delta/trend to at least one KPI to satisfy the C3 'label + value + delta + trend' bar; otherwise the KPI row reads as placeholder counts.

sub_feature: Bulk actions (Acknowledge / Resolve / Dismiss / floating selection bar)
target_gap: A wired multi-select (checkboxes + select-all) populating selectedIds so the bulk-action bar and the three bulk server actions actually run.
evidence: const [selectedIds, setSelectedIds] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set()); — every reference to setSelectedIds in this file sets `new Set()` (lines 433,650,701,715,1144,1244,1292); there is NO checkbox, no select-all, no per-row select handler, and InsightCard exposes no selection prop. The toolbar gets selectedCount={selectedIds.size} (always 0), so Toolbar's bulk bar (hasSelection = selectedCount>0) never renders and bulkActions {Acknowledge/Resolve/Dismiss} (lines 1038-1065) are permanently unre
recommendation: Add a real selection affordance: give InsightCard a `selected`/`onSelectToggle` prop (a checkbox in the lead column) wired to setSelectedIds, plus a select-all in the grouped/table headers. Then the existing bulk bar + bulkAcknowledge/Resolve/DismissInsights actions become reachable. Until then the bulk feature is dead UI.

target_gap: The FairwayBrief category deep-link must pre-apply the category filter on the live surface (param key alignment).
evidence: FairwayBrief.tsx:174 links to `/golf/dashboard/insights?category=${token}`. page.tsx (redesign branch) destructures `category` out and folds it into `categoryChips`: `categoryChips: Array.from(new Set([...]))`. But the live component reads ONLY `sp.category` — `parseSetParam(sp.category)` (line 283) and `if (!sp.category && defaultFilter.categories?.length)` (line 308). It never reads `categoryChips`. So the folded value lands in a key the live surface ignores → the deep-linked category filter n
recommendation: In the redesign branch of page.tsx, pass the deep-link through as `category` (the key the live component reads) — e.g. keep `category` as-is or merge into a `category` CSV — rather than renaming it to the legacy `categoryChips`. (`tee` is a valid InsightCategory, so once the key matches the filter works.)

sub_feature: Row card click vs. row action buttons (nested interactive)
target_gap: Action clicks must not also trigger the card-open handler, and interactive controls must not be nested inside a role='button' container.
evidence: renderCard sets `interactive onClick={() => setOpenRowId(row.id)}` on InsightCard, and InsightCard renders `actions` (the Acknowledge/Dismiss/Focus-area <Button>s) INSIDE the same <article> that gets `role='button'` + `tabIndex={0}`. The action buttons have no e.stopPropagation, so clicking 'Create focus area' or a pattern 'Confirm' (neither removes the row) ALSO fires the card's setOpenRowId → the InsightPanel sheet pops open at the same time as navigating/confirming. Nesting <button>s inside a
recommendation: Stop event propagation on every row action handler (onClick={(e)=>{e.stopPropagation(); handler();}}), and make the card's open affordance a dedicated element (e.g. the title/body region or an explicit 'Open' control) rather than wrapping the whole article — so the card is not a role='button' that contains buttons.

sub_feature: Per-row triage feedback (acknowledge / dismiss / create focus area)
target_gap: Visible success + failure feedback (Nielsen #1/#9) on the per-row triage actions, with undo where applicable.
evidence: removeInsightOptimistic: on `!res.success` it does `setInsights(prev)` (row silently reappears) with NO error notice or toast. handleCreateFocusAreaFromInsight only sets error on a thrown exception, and on success silently router.push — no success confirmation. Bulk path uses setNotice(...) for success, but the per-row path (the common case) gives no visible success/failure feedback at all. A coach who dismisses a row that fails server-side just sees it flicker back with no explanation.
recommendation: On per-row action failure, surface the returned error via the existing InlineNotice/toast (the action already returns {success,error}); on success show a brief confirmation/undo ('Acknowledged · Undo'). Wire the same notice channel the bulk path uses (setNotice/setError).

target_gap: Empty-state copy/CTA must match what this route can actually do (a real next action, not a phantom 'Scan').
evidence: The non-filtered insights empty state reads: title 'All clear — no signals right now', description 'Your players are on track. Scan the team to check for anything new.' But /insights renders with showScanTeam=false (page.tsx never passes it), so there is NO Scan-Team control on this route. The copy instructs the coach to perform an action the surface does not offer.
recommendation: Either render an actual CTA here (e.g. a Scan-Team button or a link to where scanning lives) or change the copy to something achievable on this route (e.g. 'New insights appear here as players log rounds — check the Brief or run a team scan from Alerts.'). An empty state should offer a real next action (hard-gate B2).

sub_feature: Data completeness — limit:100 truncation, no pagination/total disclosure
target_gap: No silent truncation: paginate or honestly disclose loaded-vs-total when the visible set exceeds the 100 cap.
evidence: loadInsights calls getInsightsForCoach(coachId, { limit: 100 }). getInsightsForCoach clamps limit to 100 and slices the ranked full set to 100 (the action even logs a soft-ceiling warning at >800 visible rows). The surface has NO pagination / load-more (grep for pagination/loadMore returns nothing). The only disclosure is a 'Loaded' MetricCard counting allRows (max 100) — it never states the true eligible total, so a team with >100 visible insights silently loses rows with no '100 of N' indicato
recommendation: Either paginate (load-more past the first 100) or, at minimum, surface the true eligible count vs loaded ('Showing 100 of N — load more') so the cap is honest. The legacy page paginated within the set; the premium path should not silently truncate.

sub_feature: Touch targets — primary row/bulk action buttons
target_gap: Primary triage action buttons reach >=44px touch height on mobile.
evidence: Fairway Button size='sm' = 'min-h-[36px] px-3.5 py-1.5' (button.tsx:87) — below the 44px premium/touch bar. All per-row triage actions (Confirm/Address/Resolve/Dismiss/Focus area/Acknowledge) and the bulk-action buttons are rendered with size='sm'. These are the coach's most-tapped controls on a triage surface.
recommendation: Use size='md' (min-h-44px) for the primary per-row triage actions on touch, or bump the sm token to >=44px on coarse pointers. The DoD requires touch targets >=44px.

sub_feature: Touch targets — applied-filter chip remove buttons
target_gap: Chip dismiss targets meet WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 (>=24px), premium would be 44px.
evidence: The applied-filter recall Chips (severity/status/category) render a remove <button> sized 'h-4 w-4' (sm) / 'h-5 w-5' (md) = 16-20px (badge.tsx:96-97). That is below WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 minimum target size (24x24) and far below the 44px premium bar. SignalsToolbar renders these chips with size='sm'.
recommendation: Increase the chip remove hit area to >=24px (ideally 44px via padding) while keeping the glyph small, e.g. enlarge the clickable button padding without changing the visual icon size.

target_gap: A manual refresh (and AI-settings link) so the coach can re-pull the feed without a triage side-effect.
evidence: The legacy InsightsPageContent header offers Generate (generateTeamInsights), a Refresh control, and an AI-settings link. The live FairwayCoachHelmSignals has NO refresh button (data only re-reads after a triage/bulk action or scan) and NO generate or AI-settings entry point on /insights. A coach who wants to re-pull or regenerate has no control; the surface can only be re-fetched implicitly.
recommendation: Add at least a Refresh control (re-run loadInsights(false)) and a quiet link to coaching-intelligence settings to the CoachHelmShell actions slot, matching the legacy parity. Decide intentionally whether Generate belongs here or only on the Brief.

sub_feature: Export — degrades silently from selection to 'export all filtered'
target_gap: Export communicates its scope (selected vs all-filtered) and respects selection once selection exists.
evidence: handleExport: `const ids = selectedIds.size > 0 ? Array.from(selectedIds) : filteredRows.map(r => r.id)`. Because selection is dead (finding 1), the first branch is unreachable, so Export ALWAYS exports the full filtered set with no indication to the coach that it's exporting everything (no 'Export N' label, no confirm). The Export button label is just 'Export'.
recommendation: Once selection is wired, label the Export button with the count ('Export 12') and/or confirm the scope. Until then, label it 'Export all (N)' so the coach knows the scope.

target_gap: The expand-in-place read shows the data it already loaded (timestamp, drills, resolved player) rather than a near-empty detail.
evidence: The expand-in-place InsightPanel detail block only renders `Player: {playerName}` for insights — and for insights the adapter sets playerName=undefined (patternToInsightVocabulary.ts:223), so the detail line is empty for the insights source. The panel carries no timestamp, no category/status chip, and no attached-drill chips even though getInsightsForCoach pre-joins golf_drills (INSIGHT_SELECT includes drill_attachments). The richest 'read' of a signal omits data the read already fetched.
recommendation: Surface created-at, status, and the pre-fetched drill chips in the panel detail; resolve a player name for insights (the surface has filterOptions players elsewhere / can join) so the 'Player:' line isn't blank.

sub_feature: Grouped 'By player' header — Unknown player fallback
target_gap: Insights rows carry resolved player names so the default 'By player' grouping is meaningful instead of one 'Unknown player' bucket.
evidence: For the insights source, insightToSignalRow sets playerName=undefined (line 223), so grouping 'By player' (the default groupBy for insights, line 296) buckets EVERY insight row under the single 'Unknown player' heading (line 800 fallback). The default grouped view of the insights surface therefore collapses the whole feed into one meaningless 'Unknown player' group.
recommendation: Resolve player names for the insights source (join golf_players in getInsightsForCoach, or map via the filterOptions players the page already loads) so 'By player' grouping actually groups by athlete; otherwise default insights to groupBy='category'.

target_gap: No link that points back to the same page implying a different 'archive'.
evidence: On the insights surface, a footer link reads 'Looking for the full archive? Open the insight workspace' → href '/golf/dashboard/insights' — i.e. it links back to the SAME route the coach is already on (the live insights surface is itself this component). The 'full archive' it implies (the legacy paginated InsightsPageContent) only renders when the redesign flag is OFF, so on the live path the link is a no-op self-reference.
recommendation: Remove this self-referential link on the live path, or point it at a genuinely different destination (e.g. an archive view with resolved/dismissed history). As-is it implies a richer archive that the premium path doesn't reach.

target_gap: Hard gate B3 requires every error state to offer retry. Add an in-UI retry control to reach Layer 3.
evidence:
if (loaderError) { return (
{loaderError}. Refresh the page to try again — ...
); } — the notice has NO action/retry button; it only tells the user to refresh the page manually.
recommendation: Give the SSR error path a real recovery: pass an `action` to InlineNotice with a button (e.g. a client 'Try again' that router.refresh()s, or render this through the client FairwayEffectiveness so its existing handleRefresh retry is reachable). Never ship an error state whose only 'fix' is the browser reload.

sub_feature: CoachHelm sub-nav (primary navigation on this surface)
target_gap: Fix the ARIA role mismatch so screen readers announce a navigation list of links (not an empty tablist). Required for Layer 3 a11y.
evidence: <ul role="tablist"> ... <li role="presentation"> <Link ... aria-current={isActive?'page':undefined} tabIndex=...> — the items are Next <Link>s with NO role="tab" and NO aria-selected. A role="tablist" with non-tab children is an invalid ARIA pattern (WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value); these are also real route-navigating links, not tabs.
recommendation: Drop role="tablist"/role="presentation". The element is already wrapped in <nav aria-label>; render a plain <ul>/<li> of links and keep aria-current="page" on the active one. (If a tab pattern is truly wanted, switch to button-driven panels with role="tab"+aria-selected — but for cross-route links, the nav/link semantics are correct.)

target_gap: Numbers must be honestly labelled with the window they describe; remove the hardcoded 30-day caption to reach Layer 3 data-honesty.
evidence: Line 415: Validated predictions · last 30 days and line 437: `Awaiting resolved predictions — ${resolved} of ${GAUGE_MIN_RESOLVED}.` while the header (line 261) correctly reads `Last ${days} days`. With the date-range Segmented set to 7d/14d/60d/90d the hero still hardcodes 'last 30 days', contradicting the active range.
recommendation: Thread the active range (days) into PrimaryInstrument and render `last ${days} days` instead of the literal 30. Same for any other 30-day literal so the caption never contradicts the selected filter.

sub_feature: Insights-surfaced tertiary readout vs selected range
target_gap: Make every cockpit figure reflect the selected range (no fixed-30d leak) for Layer 3 data correctness.
evidence: getCoachHelmOverview hardcodes a 30-day window (`const thirtyDaysAgo = ...`) and is NOT re-fetched on range change (handleRange only re-fetches effectiveness/performance/patternImpact, lines 215-219; overview is only refreshed by handleRefresh). InsightsSurfacedReadout falls back to `overview?.totalInsights` (line 614) — a fixed 30-day count — even when the user has selected 7d, so 'Insights surfaced' can show a 30-day figure under a 'Last 7 days' header.
recommendation: Either (a) make getCoachHelmOverview accept a DateRange and re-fetch it on range change, or (b) drive 'Insights surfaced' solely from the range-scoped effectiveness.overall.totalGenerated and drop the 30-day overview fallback so the count always matches the active window.

sub_feature: Accuracy summary windowing (rate vs count mismatch)
target_gap: Align the rate and the count to one window so the stated payoff sentence is arithmetically true.
evidence: summary.overallAccuracy = rateTotals.accuracy / count (AVERAGE of accuracy_rate across ALL rolling snapshots) while summary.validatedPredictions = (latest?.predictions_validated) (LATEST snapshot only). The hero then states `of ${resolved} resolved predictions proved accurate` (FairwayEffectiveness.tsx:436) — pairing an all-snapshot averaged rate with a single-snapshot count, two different denominators.
recommendation: Compute overallAccuracy and the 'resolved' count over the SAME basis (e.g. weight accuracy by each snapshot's validated count, or report both from the latest snapshot). The sentence 'X% of N resolved proved accurate' should use one coherent window.

target_gap: Use the design-system Readout / a scale-step size (≤3 sizes, token-only) to reach Layer 3 foundation discipline.
evidence: {live ? formatPercent(accuracy, 0) : '—'} — an arbitrary off-scale type size hand-rolled inline, bypassing the Readout primitive's SIZE_VALUE map (sm/md/lg/hero = 28/40/56/72px). 64px is on no scale step.
recommendation: Render the hero via the Readout primitive (state live/awaiting, size lg or hero, display=formatPercent) so the value, awaiting state, and type scale all come from one source — and the bespoke 'live ? … : —' / lowConfidence logic stops duplicating the Readout's honesty contract. At minimum use a token size step, not text-[64px].

target_gap: A real, reachable first-run empty state (one message + next action) instead of dead code, for Layer 3 completeness.
evidence: if (!overview && !effectiveness && !performance && !patternImpact) { return <EmptyState title="No effectiveness signal yet" ... /> } — but all four loaders return success:true with ZEROED objects on empty (generateMockInsightEffectiveness/generateMockPredictionPerformance at lines 841/874/982/1013; getPatternImpact returns a zeroed object at 479). So on a real load these props are never all undefined; this EmptyState is effectively dead code and the user instead sees a grid of 'awaiting' instrum
recommendation: Either derive the genuinely-empty condition from the actual zero aggregates (e.g. totalGenerated===0 && validatedPredictions===0 && patternsDetected===0) to show the friendly EmptyState+CTA, or delete the dead branch. As-is a brand-new team sees a cockpit of dim gauges rather than one clear 'no signal yet, here's how to start' moment.

target_gap: Primary filter/refresh controls at >=44px on touch to reach Layer 3 mobile parity.
evidence: The range Segmented is size="sm" → items are min-h-[30px] (segmented.tsx:53) and the Refresh Button is size="sm" → min-h-[36px] (button.tsx:87). Both sit in the masthead action cluster as the primary interactive controls of the surface; 30px/36px are below the 44px premium tap target (DoD 'touch targets >=44px').
recommendation: Use size="md" for the range Segmented (min-h-[36px]) and Refresh on touch viewports, or bump the sm step to >=44px for these masthead controls. They are the most-used controls on the page and should clear the premium tap bar on mobile.

sub_feature: Strokes-gained tornado a11y vs documented behavior
target_gap: Doc/impl parity; optional per-row keyboard focus would push toward Layer 4.
evidence: Header doc: 'Keyboard-focusable rows announce their value via the row's aria-label' — but the implementation renders <svg ... aria-hidden> (line 143) with NO focusable rows and NO per-row aria-label. The chart is only reachable via ChartFrame's 'view as table' toggle + the figure-level aria-label.
recommendation: The table fallback makes this acceptable, but either implement the focusable annotated rows the doc promises or correct the comment so future maintainers don't assume per-row keyboard access exists. (Low because the figure is still fully accessible via the table.)

target_gap: Keep the documentation in sync with the implementation; purely internal polish.
evidence: The file header (lines 19-25) describes the PRIMARY instrument as 'a sweeping RadialGauge of overall prediction ACCURACY (climbing toward ~70%) with the huge mono readout', but the shipped PrimaryInstrument comment at 411-412 states 'Flat, clean hero — a big SF/mono number, NOT a gauge.' The extensive cockpit doc no longer matches the implementation.
recommendation: Update the file-header narrative to match the shipped flat-number hero (and remove the RadialGauge/Dial language) so the spec block is trustworthy. Not user-facing, but a craft/maintainability tell.

target_gap: Add a completion confirmation / freshness timestamp to fully satisfy visibility-of-system-status; nudges toward Layer 4.
evidence: Refresh shows 'Refreshing…' and disables (good), and isPending swaps the body to CockpitSkeleton (281-282). But there is no success confirmation toast/'updated just now' timestamp after a manual Refresh — the user can't tell whether anything changed when the numbers are identical. lastUpdated exists on overview (action line 761) but is never surfaced.
recommendation: On successful refresh, show a subtle 'Updated <relative time>' line (use overview.lastUpdated) or a brief toast, so Refresh gives visible completion feedback (Nielsen #1 visibility of system status) even when the data is unchanged.

target_gap: Add a designed error state with retry for the philosophy fetch/create failure path; never let a load failure render as a perpetual skeleton.
evidence: const { philosophy, loading, saving, save } = useCoachPhilosophy(coachId); — `error` is exposed by the hook (useCoachPhilosophy.ts:131,222 returns `error`) but never destructured or rendered. The guard `if (loading || !philosophy) return <skeleton>` (line 197) means a failed fetch/create (hook sets error + loading=false, philosophy stays null) renders the loading skeleton FOREVER with no message, no retry.
recommendation: Destructure `error` from the hook and render a real error state (InlineNotice tone=danger + a Retry that re-runs the fetch) when error && !loading && !philosophy, instead of falling through to the infinite skeleton. target_gap: Every interactive control must reach a real consumer; remove or wire the dead Bubble Zone slider.

evidence: The only control to switch calendar views uses Segmented at default size md = min-h-[36px] (and sm=30px). WCAG 2.2 AA (2.5.8) and the rubric require >=44px touch targets. On mobile this is the single most-used calendar control and it is 36px tall.
recommendation: Bump the Segmented md size to min-h-[44px] (or render the calendar's view toggle at a 44px size), keeping the segment hit area >=44px tall on touch.

target_gap: Availability busy periods are bucketed by the viewer's local day; no off-by-one-day shift.
evidence: const r = await getPlayerAvailability(id, s, e); — the third positional timezoneOffset arg is omitted. getPlayerAvailability (golf.ts:3446-3454) documents: 'omitted -> UTC day'. So the coach availability overlay (their flagship 'find common free time' feature) anchors each player's busy window to the UTC day, not the coach's local day. In western timezones an evening event can land on the wrong day in the overlay.
recommendation: Pass new Date().getTimezoneOffset() as the 4th arg: getPlayerAvailability(id, s, e, new Date().getTimezoneOffset()), consistent with how other callers anchor to the viewer's local day.

sub_feature: Create / Edit / Delete / RSVP — success feedback (visibility of system status)
target_gap: Every successful mutation gives an explicit, consistent visible confirmation.
evidence: grep 'toast.' across src/components/fairway/pages/calendar returns nothing. After a successful create/edit, the editor closes and router.refresh() runs with no confirmation. After RSVP, the drawer just soft-closes 240ms later (setTimeout(() => onOpenChange(false), 240)). No 'Event created' / 'Response saved' toast. The legacy AttendancePanel DOES use toasts, making the absence inconsistent.
recommendation: Fire a Sonner toast on success ('Practice created', 'You're going', 'Event cancelled', 'Series updated') from handleSaveEvent/handleDeleteEvent/handleRestoreEvent and the player RSVP path. The app already wires Sonner globally.

sub_feature: Event editor — date/time inputs on narrow mobile
target_gap: Editor date/time fields stack to one column under ~360px with no clipping.
evidence: The date well, time well, RSVP deadline/max, and recurrence end/count rows all use 'grid grid-cols-2 gap-3' with no sm: breakpoint. On a 320px-wide screen a native type='date'/type='time' control plus a 12px label in a half-width column is cramped (native pickers have a hard minimum width and the date text can clip). There is no single-column fallback.
recommendation: Use 'grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-3' for these paired rows so they stack on the narrowest screens, matching the attendee grid which already does grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3.

sub_feature: Coach 'New event' on Week/Month vs the legacy grid create flow
target_gap: Exactly one create UI on every calendar view.
evidence: The hero 'New event' opens the native FairwayEventEditor (openCreate). The embedded legacy grid simultaneously exposes its own QuickAddEventFAB and grid '+'/N-key create, which open the legacy EventDetailModal. So a coach on Week/Month has two DIFFERENT create UIs reachable at once (native Fairway editor vs legacy modal), with different look and different field sets. Confusing and non-premium.
recommendation: Suppress the legacy create entry points (FAB, grid '+', N-key) when mounted inside the Fairway shell so the Fairway editor is the single create surface, or remove the legacy grid entirely (see top finding).

target_gap: Selects styled consistently with Fairway inputs (custom chevron, tokenized).
evidence: Recurrence frequency and 'Series ends' use bare native <select className={fieldCls}>. fieldCls has no appearance-none/custom chevron, so the dropdown renders with the OS default chevron and OS option styling — visually inconsistent with the rest of the Fairway forms (which elsewhere use Base UI controls). Not broken, but reads less premium than the surrounding tokenized inputs.
recommendation: Wrap in the Fairway Select primitive, or add appearance-none + a lucide ChevronDown overlay so the control matches Fairway styling.

target_gap: Subscribe sheet has a designed empty state, not just a child component default.
evidence: When feeds load successfully but the list is empty (no feed created yet), the Sheet shows the CalendarFeedManager with the create affordance but no explicit Fairway empty-state framing/illustration; the intro paragraph (line 1035) is the only guidance. The error path (feedsError) and loading path (Skeleton) are designed, but the genuinely-empty state leans on a generic child.
recommendation: Confirm CalendarFeedManager renders a helpful empty state with showNameInput=false; if not, add a one-line Fairway empty hint above the create button ('You don't have a feed yet — create one to sync to your phone').

sub_feature: Drawer location link — full-width tap target / label
target_gap: External map link announces destination + new-tab behavior to AT.
evidence: The location row is an <a> that opens Google Maps in a new tab with no aria-label indicating it opens externally / in a new tab (only a decorative ExternalLink icon aria-hidden). Screen-reader users hear the address text but not that activating it leaves the app.
recommendation: Add aria-label={`Open ${event.location} in Google Maps (opens in a new tab)`} on the anchor.

sub_feature: Keyboard navigation parity on coach Week/Month
target_gap: One keyboard owner for calendar navigation; no two-state desync.
evidence: The Fairway shell binds global ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/T to navigate(). On coach Week/Month the legacy PremiumCalendarClient ALSO binds its own keyboard handlers (onViewDay/Week/Month at lines 555-557 and its own nav). Two independent keyboard owners on the same screen can both react to the same key and desync the two date states.
recommendation: Once the duplicate-chrome finding is resolved (single grid owner), ensure only one keyboard handler owns calendar navigation; suppress the Fairway-shell key handler while the legacy grid is mounted (currently only suppressed while the drawer is open).

sub_feature: Coach roster card · Avg Score stat
target_gap: Honest, un-truncated Avg Score (paginated or DB-aggregated) — a data-correctness hard gate (B4).
evidence: const { data: allRounds } = await supabase.from('golf_rounds').select('player_id, total_score, holes_played').in('player_id', playerIds).not('total_score', 'is', null);  — no .limit(), no .range()/fetchAllRows pagination. avg_score per card is derived from this set.
recommendation: Paginate this query past the PostgREST 1000-row hard cap (use the project's fetchAllRowsResult / .order('id').range(...) helper) OR aggregate per-player server-side via an RPC/SQL SUM/COUNT so the Avg Score reflects ALL rounds. Until then the headline number on every card silently lies for high-volume teams.

target_gap: A skeleton that matches the live Fairway content (no layout swap / CLS on hydrate) — Layer-3 'three states designed, not default' (B3).
evidence: return <RosterPageSkeleton />;  — RosterPageSkeleton (src/components/ui/skeleton.tsx:1520) renders a max-w-7xl, single-column list of 8 HORIZONTAL rows with a 12px avatar, THREE fake stat columns and a 'border-white' status ring. The live page (FairwayCoachRoster) renders a max-w-[1200px] 2-COLUMN grid of tall matte cards each with ONE Avg Score stat. The skeleton predicts neither layout.
recommendation: Add a Fairway-shaped skeleton that mirrors the 2-col card grid (68-76px avatar, name+year row, status+intent chips, single Avg Score plinth, full-width CTA) for the coach view, and a teammate-card skeleton for the player view. Branch in loading.tsx (or move skeletons into the components) so the skeleton matches whichever role renders.

target_gap: RFC-4180-correct escaping + injection guard so Export produces a faithful, safe file — Layer-3 data honesty.
evidence: const csv = [headers, ...rows].map(row => row.map(cell => `"${cell}"`).join(',')).join('\n');  — cells are wrapped in quotes but embedded double-quotes are NOT doubled (a hometown/name containing " breaks the column), and there is no neutralization of cells starting with =,+,-,@ (CSV/formula injection when opened in Excel/Sheets).
recommendation: Escape inner quotes by doubling (cell.replace(/"/g,'""')) and prefix any cell beginning with =,+,-,@ (or tab/CR) with a leading apostrophe/space to defuse formula injection. This is shared by the Fairway Export button (FairwayCoachRoster.tsx:103 imports it verbatim).

sub_feature: Player status badge · popover menu semantics
target_gap: ARIA pattern that matches actual keyboard behavior (arrow-key operable menu, or honest non-menu role) — WCAG 2.2 / Nielsen #4 consistency.
evidence: aria-haspopup="menu" on the trigger and <div role="menu"> + PopoverPanel.Item role="menuitemradio" aria-checked — but PopoverPanel (src/components/fairway/overlays/PopoverPanel.tsx:23) is built on @radix-ui/react-popover, which has NO arrow-key roving menu navigation. The component header even states it 'does NOT lock scroll or trap focus'.
recommendation: Either rebuild this on Radix DropdownMenu (which provides menu role + arrow-key roving + typeahead for free), or drop the role="menu"/menuitemradio/aria-haspopup="menu" ARIA and present it as a labeled listbox/radiogroup the Popover actually supports. The kebab menu (FairwayPlayerActionsMenu) is fine because it does NOT claim role=menu.

target_gap: Guaranteed no-horizontal-scroll sort control at 360px — Layer-3 mobile parity (E.RESPONSIVE).
evidence: <Segmented size="sm" options=[Name, Avg score, Handicap, Rounds] /> with no fullWidth and no overflow-x. Segmented (controls/segmented.tsx:85) is a fixed inline-flex pill with no overflow-x-auto. Four labels in one pill can exceed a ~360px viewport; the parent toolbar wraps the whole pill but the pill itself cannot scroll if it overflows.
recommendation: Add overflow-x-auto (with -mx gutter) to the Segmented wrapper on small screens, or collapse the sort to a compact Select/dropdown below ~480px. Verify on a 360px viewport that all four labels are reachable without horizontal page scroll.

target_gap: Optimized, dimensioned avatar images (no CLS, lazy, responsive) — Layer-3 perf-optimized.
evidence: — raw with empty alt, no width/height attributes, no loading="lazy". The legacy/flag-off page used next/image with width/height (page.tsx:444). The Fairway re-skin regressed to raw .
recommendation: Use next/image (or at minimum set explicit width/height + loading="lazy" + decoding="async") to prevent layout reflow and unoptimized payloads on rosters with many photos. Empty alt is acceptable (name is adjacent) but the dimensions/lazy gap is a perf/CLS tell.

sub_feature: Intent control · 'No intent' cold-start chip tap target
target_gap: All interactive triggers >=24px (ideally 44px) — WCAG 2.2 target size.
evidence: Cold-start chip sizing: size==='md' ? 'h-6 ...' : 'h-5 ...' — i.e. 24px or 20px tall. The chip is the inner span; it is wrapped in a focusable <button> with no min-height, so on the small card variant (size="sm", used in FairwayPlayerCard:87) the interactive target is ~20px tall, under the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum.
recommendation: Give the wrapping <button> a min-h-[24px] (preferably min-h-[36px]/min-h-11 with negative margin so visual size is unchanged) so the intent trigger meets WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24px) target size in the sm card context.

target_gap: Helpful empty state with a real next action (B2/D10) — Layer-3 empty-state-with-CTA.
evidence: EmptyState title="No teammates yet" description="Your team roster is empty. Your coach will add players to the team." — no actionable next step for the player and no link (e.g. to Team Hub or messaging the coach). Acceptable since players cannot invite, but it is a pure dead-end empty.
recommendation: Add a soft next action (e.g. 'Message your coach' or a link to the Team page) so the empty state is not a terminal dead-end. Confirm copy matches reality: if a solo player is the only member, 'Your coach will add players' may be wrong for a player who IS effectively alone with a coach.

target_gap: Search/filter for the list (handles 10x data) — Layer-3 'search/filter works' + flexibility.
evidence: Renders sorted.map(...) into a 2-col card grid with NO pagination, virtualization, or search/filter. College rosters are small (~8-15) so this is fine today, but there is no search box and no filter (only client-side sort), so a coach overseeing multiple squads or a large dev roster has no way to find a player except scroll.
recommendation: Add a name search/filter input to the toolbar (alongside Sort + Export) for parity with other list surfaces; consider a status filter (Active/Inactive). Low priority given typical roster size, but a search is the expected affordance for a 'roster' list (Nielsen #6/#7).

sub_feature: Change-status modal · option list keyboard semantics
target_gap: Correct single-select ARIA (radiogroup) for the status picker — recognition/consistency (D4/D6).
evidence: The two status options are raw <button aria-pressed={active}> rows inside a plain <div>. A single-select choice is modeled as two independent toggle buttons (aria-pressed) rather than a radiogroup, so a screen reader does not announce '1 of 2' / grouped single-select.
recommendation: Wrap in role="radiogroup" with role="radio" + aria-checked on each option (or reuse the Fairway RadioGroup used by the IntentSheet) so the mutually-exclusive choice is announced correctly. Visual unchanged.

target_gap: Both modal flows must render in Fairway tokens/typography so the feature reads as one finished product, not a redesigned shell wrapping legacy dialogs.
evidence: FairwayMessages renders the UNCHANGED legacy modal: imports Drawer/SearchBar/Avatar/Button/EmptyState from '@/components/ui/*' and uses legacy colors throughout — bg-amber-50 border-amber-200, text-amber-800, text-warm-900, bg-primary-50, divide-warm-100, w-1.5 h-1.5 bg-primary-600 skeleton-shimmer. Inside the .fairway-ds bg-canvas page this is a different visual language (no fw tokens, no Fraunces, square Drawer chrome).
recommendation: Re-skin the New message picker onto Fairway primitives (fairway/overlays Sheet/Dialog + fairway/controls Button/Avatar/Badge + fairway/feedback EmptyState + fw tokens), or build a FairwayNewMessageSheet. The two entry points to the whole feature must match the redesign.

sub_feature: Team broadcast / group-create modal (coach-only secondary CTA)
target_gap: Coach broadcast flow must use the Fairway design system; current legacy palette/chrome fails C2 token discipline and Nielsen #4 consistency.
evidence: Also UNCHANGED legacy chrome: bg-red-50 border-red-200 text-red-700 error box, bg-warm-50 rounded-xl preview, bg-white rounded-full chips, bg-primary-100 text-primary-700 suggestion pills, w-1.5 h-1.5 bg-white skeleton-shimmer spinner — all legacy ui/* + emerald/legacy palette inside the Fairway page.
recommendation: Re-skin to Fairway tokens (fw-danger-bg, surface-tint, accent-*, Fraunces) and Fairway overlay primitives. Mirror the AskWorkspace overlay pattern so the broadcast composer matches the inbox it lives in.

target_gap: Hard-gate B3 requires a real error state (explains + retry) that never masquerades as a cheerful empty. Currently there is no error path at all in the rail.
evidence: On RPC/query error the hook does `setConversations([]); setLoading(false); return;` with no error flag exposed. MessageConversationRail then renders the cheerful EmptyState 'No conversations yet — Reach out to a teammate…'. A backend failure is indistinguishable from a true empty inbox.
recommendation: Return an `error` state from useGolfConversations and render a Fairway error state in the rail ('Couldn’t load conversations' + Retry that calls refetch). Same for a genuine empty vs failure distinction.

target_gap: B3 error-state gate: the thread must show a recoverable error on fetch failure, not a success-styled empty state.
evidence: fetchMessages destructures only `{ data }` (error ignored) and does `setMessages(((data||[]) ...).reverse())`. A failed fetch yields []; MessageThreadPane shows the honest-empty 'No messages yet — Start the conversation' even though the load failed.
recommendation: Capture the query error, expose it from the hook, and render a thread error state with Retry. Distinguish 'truly empty thread' from 'failed to load this thread'.

target_gap: B2 sub-feature completeness: a search capability is implied (action shipped) but absent in the UI; a premium inbox needs find/filter for non-trivial thread counts.
evidence: A hardened searchGolfMessages action exists (src/app/actions/messages.ts:937 — participant-scoped, wildcard-escaped, 50-row cap) and is exported, but the Fairway path imports NO search and renders NO search UI (grep for SearchBar/onSearch in pages/messages returns nothing). The rail has no way to find a message or filter conversations.
recommendation: Add a Fairway search field to the rail (or ViewHeader) wired to searchGolfMessages, with result rows that select the conversation + scroll to the matched message. At minimum add a client-side conversation filter.

target_gap: B1/B2: notifications must deep-link to the correct conversation. Right now the link ignores its target — the user must re-find the thread manually.
evidence: In-app notif sets action_url: `/golf/dashboard/messages` (no conversation id); push notifyNewMessage/sendPushNotification carry no thread route. There is no golf `messages/[id]` route (only baseball has one). FairwayMessages only reads ?player= and otherwise auto-selects conversations[0], so clicking a 'New message from X' notification opens the most-recent thread, not the one that fired it.
recommendation: Add a golf /dashboard/messages/[id] route (or accept ?conversation= in FairwayMessages) that pre-selects that thread; set action_url + push deep-link to include the conversation id.

target_gap: Nielsen #5 error prevention + #9 recoverable errors: enforce/communicate the limit client-side so the failure never reaches the server as an opaque toast.
evidence: The textarea has no maxLength, no character counter, and no client guard; server caps at 5000 (action-schemas.ts:42 content max(5000)). A user pasting/typing >5000 chars only learns on submit via a generic 'Failed to send message' toast.
recommendation: Add maxLength=5000 (or a soft counter that appears near the limit) and surface a specific message if exceeded. Prevent the error rather than reacting to it.

target_gap: DoD RESPONSIVE: touch targets >=44px on mobile. 36px meets WCAG 2.2 minimum (24px) but misses the spec's premium 44px bar for primary on-screen actions.
evidence: Mobile own-message actions (more, edit, delete, close, confirm/cancel-delete) use IconButton size="sm" which is h-9 w-9 (36px) per button.tsx:223. The legacy page used min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px] for the same controls.
recommendation: Use size="md" (44px) for the mobile action row IconButtons (the lg:hidden cluster + delete-confirm), keeping sm only for desktop hover affordances.

target_gap: DoD RESPONSIVE: mobile parity with deterministic full-width panes; current width relies on content rather than an explicit constraint.
evidence: Outer is `flex ... grid-cols-12 ... md:grid`. On mobile it is flex-row (md:grid not active); the single visible child carries `col-span-12 flex flex-col` (col-span is a no-op in flex) with NO w-full / flex-1. In a flex-row parent a content-width child is not guaranteed to span full viewport width; items-stretch only stretches the cross axis (height).
recommendation: Add `w-full` (or `flex-1`) to the aside and the thread wrapper for the mobile (flex) case, or switch the mobile container to block/grid so col-span-12 governs width deterministically.

target_gap: B4 no-data-lies: a 'Read' marker in a group must reflect honest group read state, not a single arbitrary participant.
evidence: fetchOtherParticipantReadStatus picks `participants.find(p => p.user_id !== currentUserId)` — the FIRST other participant — and marks own messages Read if created <= that single person's last_read_at. In a group/team-chat that is one arbitrary member, so 'Read' is shown when ONE (random) recipient has opened it, not all. MessageThreadPane renders this 'Read'/'Sent' for own messages in groups too.
recommendation: Either suppress per-message read receipts in is_group threads, or compute an honest aggregate (e.g. 'Read by N/total' / read only when min(last_read_at across others) >= created_at). Don’t imply group-read off one member.

target_gap: C5/DoD A11Y: honor prefers-reduced-motion on the auto-scroll, consistent with the component's own motion discipline.
evidence: scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' }) is hard-coded; it does not consult prefers-reduced-motion (the rest of the file carefully gates animation, e.g. motion-safe on the typing dots).
recommendation: Use behavior: reduced ? 'auto' : 'smooth' (read useReducedMotion or the media query) so reduced-motion users get an instant jump.

target_gap: B3 error state for the attachment sub-surface; today a failure is an eternal pending placeholder.
evidence: If getGolfMessageAttachments returns { error } (signed-URL or RLS failure), res.attachments is undefined → [] and the bubble stays on the indefinite 'Paperclip Attachment' placeholder forever with no retry or failure copy. has_attachments is true but the gallery never resolves.
recommendation: Track per-message attachment error and render a quiet 'Couldn’t load attachment — tap to retry' chip instead of a permanent loading placeholder.

target_gap: Nielsen #4 consistency / predictable ordering; minor but can surprise on a busy inbox.
evidence: Unread conversations are split into a top 'Unread' bucket; only the READ remainder is passed to groupConversationsByTime. So an unread thread from last month and an unread from today sit together under 'Unread' with no recency order guarantee beyond the hook's global sort, and they are removed from their Today/Yesterday groups — a thread can appear to 'leave' Today when it becomes unread.
recommendation: Either keep recency grouping and use the unread Badge as the only unread signal, or sort the Unread bucket by last_message time explicitly and document the dual-ordering so it stays predictable.

target_gap: C3 glass-discipline: prefer a solid surface under the scannable conversation list; currently relies on the panel being treated as chrome.
evidence: The conversation list (dense, scannable data) renders directly on an InstrumentPanel depth='base' which is a backdrop-blur frosted-glass surface (instrument-panel.module.css). Spec C3: dense data on SOLID surfaces, glass only on chrome. The thread well correctly overrides to bg-surface (solid) at MessageThreadPane.tsx:407-409, but the rail rows sit on glass.
recommendation: Borderline-acceptable since the panel is positioned as 'aside/chrome' and collapses to matte under reduced-transparency; consider a solid surface for the rail list region to fully satisfy C3.

target_gap: Honest error state that surfaces failure + offers retry, instead of a cheerful empty masking it (hard-gate B3/B6).
evidence: announcements = announcementsResult.data ?? []; — getAnnouncementsWithMeta returns {success:false, error:'Failed to load announcements'|'Not authorized for this team'} on DB/auth failure WITHOUT throwing; .data is then undefined, so on ANY backend failure the page silently falls through to the friendly 'No announcements yet' EmptyState (line 116-128 of FairwayAnnouncements). The success flag is never read; error.tsx only catches throws, so it never fires.
recommendation: Branch on announcementsResult.success. On !success, render an error state (InlineNotice tone='danger' or a Surface error block) with the action's error message and a Retry (router.refresh) — never the empty state. Distinguish 'zero announcements' (success && data.length===0) from 'failed to load' (success===false).

target_gap: Disambiguate transient failure from a legitimately empty feed.
evidence: } catch { /* Network failure — proceed with null teamId (empty state below) */ } — a failed team lookup sets teamId=null, which renders the coach 'Create announcements to keep your team informed' empty state plus a 'New Announcement' button that will then fail server-side ('Coach not assigned to a team'). The failure is invisible to the user.
recommendation: On team-resolution failure surface a distinct, recoverable notice ('Couldn't load your team — try again') rather than the new-user empty state, so the empty state is reserved for genuinely team-less / zero-announcement cases.

target_gap: Skeleton must match the loaded Fairway layout + tokens; eliminate the glass-to-matte flash and the phantom sticky header.
evidence: loading.tsx renders a sticky glass header (className="sticky top-0 ... bg-cream-100/60 backdrop-blur-sm" with a 'h-10 w-44' button) and AnnouncementCardSkeleton uses 'bg-cream-100/55 backdrop-blur-glass-prominent border-warm-200/45 ... border-l-warm-200' — the LEGACY glass design system. The loaded Fairway view (FairwayAnnouncements) has NO sticky header and uses matte <Surface> cards on bg-canvas with Fairway tokens. The skeleton neither matches the loaded layout nor the design system.
recommendation: Replace loading.tsx with a Fairway skeleton: matte Surface card placeholders matching FairwayCoach/PlayerAnnouncementCard's collapsed layout, a non-sticky ViewHeader-shaped masthead skeleton, bg-canvas, and Fairway tokens (no warm-*/backdrop-blur-glass-*). Skeleton should mirror real content shape and the live DS.

target_gap: Immediate, consistent feedback for the whole task surface (Nielsen #1 visibility of system status) within one expanded card.
evidence: myCompletedTasks is derived from detail?.tasks[].assignments[].status, but FairwayTaskItem.toggle() (line 121-131) only flips its OWN local `completed` state and calls completeAnnouncementTask — it never calls setDetail or re-runs getAnnouncementDetail. So after a player checks a task, the per-item checkbox flips but the 'Your tasks {myCompletedTasks}/{myTotalTasks}' counter (line 430) and ProgressTrack (line 435) at the top of the SAME expanded card stay stale until a full page reload.
recommendation: Lift completion state up (pass an onComplete(taskId) from the card that patches detail.tasks[].assignments for playerId), or optimistically update detail in the card so the counter + progress bar reflect the toggle immediately. Optionally call router.refresh() on success.

target_gap: No fabricated 0/0 denominators (hard-gate B4 data honesty); consistent em-dash discipline.
evidence: {ann.acknowledged_count}/{ann.total_recipients} is rendered whenever ann.requires_acknowledgement is true, with NO total_recipients>0 guard. An ack-required announcement targeting a now-empty recipient set (all recipients left, or all-team on an empty roster) renders a literal '0/0'. The same file guards tasks honestly with an em-dash (line 337: total>0 ? `${completed}/${total}` : '—') and the player card guards ack with total_recipients>0 (PlayerCard line 326), so this is an internal inconsiste
recommendation: Guard like the task counter: render the ack chip only when ann.total_recipients > 0, else show '—' or omit it. Apply the same guard to the detail view's ack count (line 389).

target_gap: Primary create flow opens to a usable height; no half-collapsed form.
evidence: <Sheet ... side="bottom"> with no peek={false} and no snapPoints. Sheet defaults (Sheet.tsx:121-123) to resolvedSnapPoints=[0.5,1] for bottom sheets, so this dense multi-field create form (title, message, priority radios, recipient picker, ack switch, attachments, inline tasks) opens to a 50% half-height peek detent — the coach sees a half-collapsed form and must drag it up to see/submit the lower fields.
recommendation: Pass peek={false} (or side="right" on desktop) so a full create form opens to its working height. A peek detent suits a detail-peek, not a primary creation flow.

target_gap: Feed honors the 1000-row cap and stays correct at 10x data (DoD: paginated past 1000).
evidence: supabase.from('golf_announcements').select('*').eq('team_id', teamId).order('published_at', {ascending:false}); — no .limit() or .range(). PostgREST hard-caps at 1000 rows (per the repo's own documented gotcha). A long-lived team will silently lose the oldest announcements past 1000, corrupting recentCount/total and the feed.
recommendation: Add a bounded .limit() (e.g. 100-200 most-recent) with load-more/infinite scroll, or paginate via fetchAllRowsResult. Also enforce limits on the recipients/acks/tasks/docs .in() fan-out queries (lines 369-393) which scale with announcement count.

target_gap: A growing feed must be searchable/filterable to stay usable (DoD: search/filter works).
evidence: The feed renders all cards in one flat list with no search box, no urgency/unread/has-tasks filter, and no sort control (coach feed preserves server date order; player feed only does an unread-first sort). For a feed that grows unboundedly, there is no way to find an old announcement or filter to 'needs acknowledgement'.
recommendation: Add a lightweight filter/search row (search by title/body, filter chips for urgency + requires-ack + has-tasks, optionally a ViewHeader segmented tab for All/Unread/Action-needed). The page already passes recentCount; a 'This week' filter is natural.

target_gap: Constrain inputs to schema limits with visible feedback; specific error messages.
evidence: Title <Input> and message <TextArea> have no maxLength and no character counter, yet createAnnouncementSchema enforces title.max(200) and body.max(10000) (announcements.ts:42-43). On overflow the server returns the generic 'Invalid input. Please check your entries.' toast (announcements.ts:295) — no field name, no limit. Input/TextArea forward ...props so maxLength is available but unused.
recommendation: Add maxLength={200}/{10000} (hard prevention) plus a subtle remaining-chars counter near the limit, and make the server validation error name the offending field. This is Nielsen #5 (error prevention) + #9 (recover from errors).

target_gap: Real-time where valuable (DoD COMMS) — especially for urgent posts.
evidence: export const revalidate = 120; and no Supabase realtime subscription anywhere in pages/announcements/** (grep for realtime/subscribe/channel returns nothing). A coach posting an urgent announcement does not push to a player's already-open feed; the player sees it only after a manual refresh or up to 120s ISR. For an 'urgent' urgency tier this is a notable gap.
recommendation: Subscribe to golf_announcements inserts for the team (a useRealtime hook already exists per CLAUDE.md) and prepend new cards / show a 'New announcement — refresh' affordance. At minimum, urgent posts should surface promptly.

target_gap: WCAG 2.2: disclosure controls programmatically associated with their region (DoD A11Y: labels/aria on controls).
evidence: The collapsed-card <button> has aria-expanded={expanded} but no aria-controls, and the expanded detail region (line 254 `{expanded && <div ...>`) has no id and no role. Screen-reader users get the expanded/collapsed state but no programmatic link to the controlled region. Same pattern in FairwayPlayerAnnouncementCard.tsx:259.
recommendation: Give the expanded region a stable id (e.g. `announcement-detail-${ann.id}`) and set aria-controls to it on the toggle button. Optionally role='region' with aria-label on the panel.

target_gap: Disabled affordances explain themselves (Nielsen #1/#9, microcopy).
evidence: Attachment buttons render disabled={!url} with 'cursor-not-allowed opacity-50' but no title/aria-describedby explaining WHY (missing file URL). A player sees a greyed, unclickable document with no reason. Coach card has the same at FairwayCoachAnnouncementCard.tsx:285.
recommendation: When url is missing, add a title/aria-label like 'File unavailable' (and ideally a tiny inline 'Unavailable' tag) so the disabled state is explained rather than mysterious.

target_gap: Sharing/visibility control surfaced to the coach (DoD COMMS: sharing/visibility correct).
evidence: The row is inserted send_push:false/send_email:false (line 120-121), then the action unconditionally dispatches BOTH email (notifyTeamAnnouncement) and push (sendBulkPushNotification) to all targets and reconciles the flags after the fact (lines 282-287). The create form (FairwayCreateAnnouncement) exposes NO toggle for the coach to choose whether to email/push — every announcement notifies everyone, including 'low' urgency.
recommendation: Either expose 'Send email'/'Send push' switches in the create Options section (the schema/flags already exist) so the coach controls delivery, or gate auto-notification by urgency. Silent always-notify on a 'low' post risks notification fatigue.

sub_feature: Player feed — sort stability across reloads
target_gap: No post-hydration reorder flash; stable, calm first paint (motion/states polish).
evidence: PlayerFeed sorts unread-first using nowTs which starts at 0 and is set in useEffect (line 165). On first paint nowTs===0 so isUnreadForPlayer returns false for time-based-unread items, and the list re-sorts after mount — causing a visible reorder flash for non-ack announcements posted within 24h.
recommendation: Compute the unread-first ordering from ack state (which is time-independent) on first paint and only refine the time-based component after mount, or render a stable order and apply an accent without reordering, to avoid the post-hydration reshuffle.

target_gap: A real error state that explains the failure and offers retry, distinct from empty — required by hard-gate B3 and DoD STATES.error.
evidence: const { tasks: realtimeTasks, stats, loading: tasksLoading, refetch } = useTaskRealtime(teamId, {...}); — the hook also returns `error` (use-task-realtime.ts:80,340 sets it on a caught throw and falls back to tasks=[]/EMPTY_STATS), but `error` is never destructured here and FairwayTasks has no error prop. On any Supabase/network failure the page renders FairwayTasks with empty tasks → the EmptyState 'No tasks yet' (FairwayTasks.tsx:195-217) shows, masking the failure.
recommendation: Destructure `error` from useTaskRealtime, pass it to FairwayTasks as a prop, and render an InlineNotice tone="danger" with a 'Try again' action wired to refetch() (the hook already exposes refetch). Never let a fetch failure fall through to the empty state.

target_gap: Visible success + failure feedback on the single most-used player action (Nielsen #1/#9, hard-gate B3 success/error).
evidence: const handleCompleteTask = async (taskId: string) => { await completeTask(taskId); await refetch(); }; — completeTask returns ActionResult {success,error} (tasks.ts:37-150) but the result is discarded. On failure (RLS denial, 'You are not assigned to this task', network) the FairwayTaskCard spinner stops and nothing changes — no toast, no message. On success there is also no confirmation toast.
recommendation: Check the result: on !success show fairwayToast.error(result.error ?? 'Could not mark complete.'); on success show fairwayToast.success('Marked complete.'). Mirror the coach create path which already toasts (FairwayCreateTaskModal.tsx:134).

target_gap: Full CRUD lifecycle for the coach — create-only with no delete/edit makes the feature look unfinished (hard-gate B2 sub-feature completeness).
evidence: FairwayTaskCard renders only a coach 'View details' expander and a player 'Mark complete' button — no delete, edit, or reminder control. The server actions deleteTask (tasks.ts:292), clearTaskReminder (tasks.ts:442), and setTaskReminder-on-existing (tasks.ts:367) exist and are wired in the baseball UI (components/baseball/tasks/TaskCard.tsx:124) but have ZERO golf UI consumers. A coach who creates a task cannot remove it, fix a typo, or change/clear its reminder.
recommendation: Add a coach overflow menu (PopoverPanel) on each task card with Edit, Set/Clear reminder, and Delete (behind a ModalShell confirm, like the template delete already does at FairwayTaskTemplateList.tsx:385). Wire to the existing deleteTask/setTaskReminder/clearTaskReminder actions + refetch.

target_gap: Honest data past 1000 rows (hard-gate B4, DoD DATA.paginated).
evidence: const { data: assignRows } = await supabase.from('golf_task_assignments').select('id, task_id, player_id, status, completed_at, player:...').in('task_id', taskIds); — no .range()/pagination. PostgREST caps at 1000 rows server-side. A team with e.g. 50 tasks x 25 players = 1250 assignment rows silently truncates → 'N of M completed' and overdue/completion stats under-report.
recommendation: Paginate the assignment fetch (fetchAllRowsResult with .order('id').range(...), the project's documented pattern for the 1000-row cap) so completion math stays correct at scale.

target_gap: Search + filter that actually filters for a coach at scale (DoD DATA.search/filter, hard-gate B2).
evidence: Only three status FilterPills (All/Active/Completed). No text search, no filter by player or category, no sort control. Tasks already carry a `category` (rendered as a Chip at line 575) and assignments per player, but a coach cannot search by title, filter to one player's tasks, or sort by due date — the list is fixed to the hook's due_date asc order.
recommendation: Add a SearchField (already a Fairway primitive) for title/description, and a category filter pill row derived from the distinct task categories. Optionally a sort toggle (due date / created).

sub_feature: Overdue stat tile + reminder color tokens
target_gap: Strict design-token discipline (criteria C2 'Design tokens only').
evidence: The file header declares 'No glass / backdrop-blur / legacy warm-/primary- classes' (line 34), yet uses text-warm-800 three times: the Overdue quick-stat number/label inside bg-fw-warning-bg (lines 348, 351) and the reminder imminent/soon color (line 567). tone.tsx defines the canonical token text-fw-warning for exactly this.
recommendation: Replace text-warm-800 with text-fw-warning (or the warning foreground token) so the warning surfaces stay on-system and contrast is token-guaranteed.

target_gap: Non-visual, non-color access to the reminder info (WCAG 2.2 1.1.1/1.4.1, DoD A11Y labels/aria).
evidence: — the only reminder affordance is an icon-only span whose Bell is aria-hidden and whose meaning lives solely in a `title` attribute. `title` on a non-interactive span is not reliably announced by screen readers, so SR users get no indication a reminder exists or when.
recommendation: Give the reminder a visible text label (e.g. 'Reminder · Today 9:00 AM') or, if icon-only, add an sr-only span / aria-label on a focusable element. Color alone (warm-800) is also not an accessible signal channel.

target_gap: Instant perceived feedback for the primary player action (criteria D1 optimistic UI, Layer 3 perf-optimized).
evidence: The card and modal comments repeatedly say 'optimistic complete' (FairwayTasks.tsx:17,455,607; FairwayCreateTaskModal docblock), but handleComplete (482-494) only sets `completing` (spinner) and awaits onComplete → completeTask round-trip → full refetch before the card changes. There is no optimistic local status flip; on a slow network the player taps and waits with a spinner.
recommendation: Either make it truly optimistic (locally flip the task to completed immediately, reconcile/rollback on the action result) or correct the inaccurate 'optimistic' comments. Pair with the success/error toast from the wiring finding above.

target_gap: Feature parity between template-created and directly-created tasks; visible priority signal.
evidence: createTask is called with `undefined` for priority (line 113, comment 'priority — defaults to normal') and the modal has no priority control. golf_tasks.priority is a real column the realtime hook reads (use-task-realtime.ts:296) and templates expose Low/Normal/High/Urgent (FairwayTaskTemplateList.tsx:53-58), but a directly-created task can never be anything but 'normal' and priority is never shown on the task card.
recommendation: Add a priority RadioGroup/Select to the create modal (parity with templates) and surface priority on the card (a Chip or accent dot) so urgent/high tasks read at a glance.

target_gap: Honest empty-vs-error distinction in the assignment picker; error-prevention on a zero-assignee create.
evidence: loadPlayers() swallows errors — `const { data: teamMembers } = await supabase...` with no error handling; on failure `players` stays []. The create modal then shows 'No players on the roster yet' (FairwayCreateTaskModal.tsx:231) even when the roster fetch merely failed, and 'Assign to All team members (0 players)' would create a task assigned to nobody with no warning.
recommendation: Handle the loadPlayers error and, if players is empty due to error vs genuinely empty, distinguish them; warn the coach before creating an 'all members = 0 players' task that would assign to no one.

sub_feature: Overdue banner action when already filtered
target_gap: The banner CTA does something useful in every state (Nielsen #1 actionable status).
evidence: The overdue InlineNotice's action is only rendered when filter !== 'active' (line 228). When the user is already on Active, the banner has no actionable affordance and just restates 'Review tasks that are past their due date' — there is no way to jump to / sort overdue items to the top.
recommendation: When on Active, replace the 'View active' action with a 'Show overdue first' sort/scroll, or surface an overdue sub-filter, so the banner stays actionable.

target_gap: No post-hydration visual flicker on task meta (Layer 3 'every state designed').
evidence: now is null until the post-mount useEffect (141-144). The reminder Bell only renders when `task.reminder_at && now` (line 559), and isOverdue requires now (476-477). So on first paint reminders are absent and overdue tasks render in neutral color, then pop in / turn red after hydration — a visible flash / minor CLS on a list of tasks.
recommendation: Compute `now` once on the server or seed it from a stable timestamp so the first paint matches; or reserve space for the reminder icon to avoid the pop-in.

target_gap: Preview and download must actually resolve to the stored file for documents uploaded through this page; add a test that uploads then signs the same object.
evidence: const urlParts = data.file_url.split('/'); const storagePath = urlParts.slice(-2).join('/'); ... storage_path: storagePath  — for a public URL .../object/public/documents/golf-documents/{teamId}/{fileName}, slice(-2) yields '{teamId}/{fileName}', DROPPING the 'golf-documents/' prefix. getPreviewUrl (line 769) then calls createSignedUrl(version.storage_path) against a path that does not exist.
recommendation: Stop reconstructing storage_path from the URL. Pass the real storagePath ('golf-documents/{teamId}/{fileName}') from uploadGolfDocument through to createGolfDocument and store it verbatim (or change uploadGolfDocument to return both file_url and storage_path). Backfill existing rows' storage_path.

target_gap: The 'Upload new version' menu action must persist a version and update the document instead of throwing.
evidence: supabase.from('golf_document_versions').insert({ document_id, version_number, file_name, file_size, mime_type, storage_path, change_notes, uploaded_by }) — no file_url, but golf_document_versions.file_url is 'text NOT NULL' (migration 20260527000000_prod_public_baseline.sql). The insert throws a not-null violation, so 'Upload new version' fails every time. Same omission in createDocument (line 263) and revertToVersion (line 601).
recommendation: Include file_url in every golf_document_versions insert (uploadNewVersion, createDocument, revertToVersion) — derive it via getPublicUrl(storagePath) as createGolfDocument already does — or drop the NOT NULL constraint and rely on storage_path. uploadNewVersion is the one wired into the live Fairway menu, so it is the priority.

target_gap: Revert must create a new version from the selected one and reflect it; today the user always gets an error.
evidence: await revertToVersion(document.id, String(revertingTo)) where revertingTo = version.version_number (an integer like 2). revertToVersion (actions/documents.ts:572-577) does .eq('id', versionId).single() — 'id' is a uuid column, not the version number. The query never matches (and Postgres errors casting '2' to uuid), so revert ALWAYS fails. VersionHistory is reused verbatim by the live FairwayDocuments page.
recommendation: Pass the version's UUID (version.id) to revertToVersion, or change revertToVersion to look up by version_number (.eq('version_number', n)). Keep the parameter name/type honest (versionId: uuid). Add a unit test for the revert round-trip.

target_gap: WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard operability + 2.4.11 focus-not-obscured: every user can preview/download a document via keyboard and on touch.
evidence: <Surface elevation="border" padding="none" interactive onClick={onPreview} ...> renders the default 'div' (no as="button", no role/tabIndex/onKeyDown) so the card is not keyboard-focusable; and the only Preview/Download buttons are in a footer div with className 'opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100 motion-reduce:opacity-100' — revealed ONLY on pointer hover (no group-focus-within, no touch fallback). A player (no coach menu) therefore has zero keyboard or touch path to preview o
recommendation: Make the card a real button (as="button" with an accessible label) OR add role/tabIndex/onKeyDown(Enter/Space) to open preview; add group-focus-within:opacity-100 to the footer affordances and make them visible on coarse-pointer/touch (e.g. always-visible on <sm, or @media(hover:none)). Don't rely on hover as the sole reveal.

target_gap: Download is a primary document action; it must be discoverable and operable for both roles on all input modalities.
evidence: The coach DropdownMenu offers Preview, Version history, Upload new version, Edit details, Move to folder, Delete — but NO Download item. Download exists only as the hover-only footer IconButton, which is unreachable on touch (see a11y finding). So on a touch device a coach can only download by opening the preview modal first.
recommendation: Add an explicit 'Download' item to the coach card menu and ensure the footer download is reachable on touch. Frequent action (download) should be a first-class, always-discoverable affordance, not hover-only.

target_gap: Download produces a saved file with the right name, not just an opened tab.
evidence: link.href = data.url (a Supabase signed URL on a different origin); link.download = doc.title. The HTML download attribute is IGNORED for cross-origin URLs, so the browser navigates/opens the file in a new context instead of saving it, and the chosen filename is not applied.
recommendation: For a true download, fetch the blob (supabase.storage.download) server-side or via the signed URL, create an object URL, and trigger the download; or set response-content-disposition=attachment on the signed URL. At minimum add target/rel and accept that it opens rather than saves, and rename the affordance to 'Open' if download can't be guaranteed.

target_gap: Loading, empty, and error are distinct designed states; a failed fetch never looks like 'no versions'.
evidence: openVersionHistory sets showVersionHistory=true immediately, then awaits getVersionHistory; on failure it does setVersions(result.success && result.versions ? result.versions : []) — an error becomes an empty array, rendering VersionHistory's 'No version history available' (a cheerful empty masking a failure). There is also no loading state: the modal opens empty, then content pops in.
