recommendation: Track loading/error explicitly: show a skeleton/spinner while fetching, and on error show an InlineNotice with a Retry. Never collapse an error into the empty state (Hard Gate B3).

target_gap: User-created folders persist (or the model is honestly communicated and non-destructive).
evidence: handleCreateFolder only does setManualFolders((prev) => [...prev, folderName]) — folders are client-only state with no DB write. The modal copy ('Folders save once a file lands in them') admits an empty folder is ephemeral; navigating into it then reloading the page makes it vanish. A coach who creates 'Practice Plans' and leaves loses it.
recommendation: Either persist folders in a real table/column so an empty folder survives reload, or make the empty-folder transience explicit and prevent the user from feeling data was lost (e.g. keep folder in URL/state, or require a file at creation). Premium apps don't silently drop user-created structure.

target_gap: List and counts remain correct beyond 1000 documents.
evidence: baseQuery selects golf_documents with .order('created_at') and no .range()/pagination; PostgREST caps at 1000 rows. A team exceeding 1000 documents would silently truncate (and the meta count would be wrong).
recommendation: Either paginate via fetchAllRowsResult/.range when count may exceed 1000, or document the cap; given the domain this is low-likelihood but the count meta should not lie.

sub_feature: Last-modified vs created date on cards
target_gap: Date reflects the latest meaningful change, not just creation.
evidence: Footer shows timeAgo(doc.created_at). After 'Upload new version' the file_size/file_url change but the card still shows the original creation time, so a freshly-updated doc reads as old. updated_at exists in golf_documents but is never selected by the page query.
recommendation: Select updated_at and show it (e.g. 'Updated 2m ago') when version_count>1, falling back to created_at otherwise; sort 'Newest' could optionally use updated_at.

target_gap: Form controls use the design-system primitive's API rather than re-styling it inline.
evidence: The search field, edit-title Input, edit-description TextArea, and new-folder Input each re-implement the Input primitive's surface/border/focus-ring with large hand-written className overrides (h-11, border-border-subtle, focus-visible:ring-accent-500/70, etc.) and a manually absolute-positioned IconSearch, instead of using Input's leading adornment slot and default styling.
recommendation: Use <Input leading={<IconSearch/>} trailing={clear} /> and the primitive's default sizing/focus for all four fields; remove the duplicated className blocks. Consistency + single source of truth for field styling.

target_gap: Every surface reachable from the live page uses Fairway tokens/primitives; no shadcn/legacy color leak.
evidence: DocumentPreview uses non-Fairway tokens (text-red-500, text-blue-500, text-purple-500, text-warm-*, bg-black, shadcn Dialog/Button) and UploadNewVersionModal uses legacy primary-*/warm-*/bg-red-50/bg-blue-50 plus a 'max 2MB' hint that doesn't match the page. These modals open from the live Fairway page, breaking the warm-matte cream design system mid-flow (glass/shadcn dialog vs Fairway ModalShell).
recommendation: Re-skin the preview and upload-new-version surfaces onto Fairway tokens/ModalShell (or wrap them) so the experience stays on-system when launched from FairwayDocuments; reconcile the file-size hint with the real limit.

sub_feature: Upload modal busy/disabled affordance vs error recovery
target_gap: Bulk upload communicates per-file outcome and supports recovering from partial failure.
evidence: Multi-file upload loops sequentially; on a mid-loop failure it sets uploadError and returns, leaving already-uploaded files committed and the remaining ones not — partial success with no per-file status or retry-failed-only. The progress bar resets to 0 in finally even after a partial commit.
recommendation: Track per-file status (queued/uploading/done/failed), allow retry of only failed files, and message partial success honestly ('3 of 5 uploaded'). Avoid leaving the user unsure what landed.

sub_feature: No-team fallback state (legacy styling on live path)
target_gap: Every page state (including the no-team guard) is on-system and offers a next action.
evidence: The 'No Team Found' branch renders text-warm-900/text-warm-600 outside the .fairway-ds scope and EmptyState system — a legacy-token, unstyled fallback that a user without a team would hit even on the redesign path, with no CTA.
recommendation: Render the no-team case inside fairwayScope using EmptyState with an action (e.g. 'Join a team') and Fairway tokens, consistent with the rest of the live path.

target_gap: Wire the file to uploadExpenseReceipt so attaching a receipt actually persists; without it the control is a lie that loses user data.
evidence: const finalReceiptUrl = receiptUrl; if (receiptFile) { /* For now, we'll handle receipt upload in a separate flow */ /* In production, you'd upload to Supabase Storage here */ } — receiptFile is then never used; uploadExpenseReceipt() (travel.ts:748) has ZERO callers (grep confirms). A coach picks a file (line 375-381), the UI shows it 'attached' with name+size (349-354), Save runs, and the receipt is silently dropped.
recommendation: On submit, when receiptFile is set, call uploadExpenseReceipt(receiptFile, teamId, expense?.id) and use the returned url as receipt_url before create/update; surface upload errors inline. Show a busy state during upload. This is the only write path for receipt_url so without it the entire 'Receipt' feature and the ExpenseList 'View receipt' viewer are dead for newly added receipts.

target_gap: A whole tab of the live premium surface is styled in the legacy non-token palette + an emoji; must be re-skinned to tokens to hit Layer 3.
evidence: CATEGORY_CONFIG uses raw hex ('#3B82F6','#8B5CF6','#F97316','#22C55E','#14B8A6','#78716c'); cards use bg-white, bg-blue-50/text-blue-900, bg-amber-50/text-amber-900, bg-gradient-to-br from-primary-50; ExpenseList.tsx:39-44 uses bg-blue-100/purple-100/orange-100/teal-100 and 💸 emoji (line 101); ExpenseForm uses warm-*/primary-* throughout. These render INSIDE the flag-on Fairway page (imported by FairwayTripDetail.tsx:41 and FairwayTravel.tsx:61).
recommendation: Re-skin the expense components to Fairway tokens (text-text-*, bg-surface/surface-sunken, accent-*, fw-warning/fw-danger, StatusPill for paid-by, no emoji) OR build Fairway-native FairwayExpenseSummary/List/Form. The docstrings claim 'Tokens ONLY … no glass/blur/warm-*/blue-*/amber-*' yet half the live screen is exactly that — failing C1 grayscale/effects-off and C2 token discipline.

sub_feature: Create/Edit modal → Link to event picker
target_gap: Round-trip the event link (read it back, show it, keep it on edit) or drop the control; currently it's a write-only field that silently resets.
evidence: The page mapper builds the TravelItinerary prop object WITHOUT event_id (no event_id key in the mapped object), so FairwayItineraryModal.itineraryToForm reads `(itinerary as { event_id?: string|null }).event_id` (FairwayItineraryModal.tsx:95) which is always undefined. event_id is written on create/update but never selected back into the prop, never displayed in FairwayTripDetail or FairwayTripCard, and on re-edit the picker defaults to 'No linked event' — silently un-linking unless the coach re
recommendation: Add event_id to the page mapper and the TravelItinerary type; prefill the picker from it; and surface the link (e.g. a 'Linked to: <event> →' row in FairwayTripDetail that deep-links to the calendar). Otherwise remove the picker — a write-only field that loses its value on edit is worse than no field.

target_gap: Conditionally render Split only when it has real data; an always-zero card for a removed feature is a data lie (B4).
evidence: A 'Split' card always renders formatCurrency(summary.byPaidBy.split), but ExpenseForm.tsx:54-63 intentionally removed the 'split' option ('Cost splitting is a deferred feature … a Split choice would be a dead end'). So for any team using the current form, Split is permanently $0 — a fabricated metric that can never be non-zero.
recommendation: Hide the Split card unless summary.byPaidBy.split > 0 (so only legacy rows show it), matching the 'honest, only > 0' pattern used in the Fairway masthead meta. Don't show an authoritative $0 for a disabled path.

target_gap: Add filter/sort (upcoming-first) + handle >100 rows; a flat capped list with most-relevant items buried is below the dense-data premium bar.
evidence: Itineraries are fetched with .limit(100) and rendered as a single flat ascending-by-departure_date list (FairwayTravel.tsx:324-332). There is NO sort control, NO filter (upcoming/past), NO search, and NO grouping. A program with a full multi-season history hits the 100 cap silently and a coach must scroll the whole list to find a past trip — past trips sit at the TOP (asc order) so the most relevant 'next trip' is buried below completed ones.
recommendation: Add at minimum an Upcoming/Past segmented filter (the data for upcoming/past counts already exists in the masthead) and default-sort upcoming-first; consider a search box. If >100 trips is realistic, paginate or window. A premium list of a core nav item should not be an unsorted/unfiltered scroll.

target_gap: Make the first-paint status honest (server now or skeleton) instead of defaulting everything to 'Upcoming'.
evidence: getTripStatus returns {label:'Upcoming', tone:'neutral'} for EVERY trip until the client `now` resolves (FairwayTravel.tsx:95-98 sets now in useEffect). So on first paint a completed/in-transit trip is briefly mislabeled 'Upcoming'. The masthead meta is hidden until now resolves (correct), but the per-card pill shows a wrong status.
recommendation: Compute initial status from a server-passed `nowISO` (date-granularity, hydration-safe) so the first paint is already correct, or render the pill skeletoned until now resolves. A flash of 'Upcoming' on a finished trip is a transient data lie.

target_gap: Add inputMode hints for numeric fields to reach mobile-parity polish.
evidence: Hotel phone uses type='tel' (ok) but the Expense amount field (ExpenseForm.tsx:283-292) is type='number' without inputMode='decimal', and several text fields (confirmation #, etc.) have no inputMode. The 19-field itinerary modal and the expense form give no explicit inputMode hints, so iOS shows the full keyboard for numeric-leaning fields.
recommendation: Add inputMode='decimal' to the amount field and inputMode='numeric' to confirmation/phone where appropriate. Minor but expected on a mobile-parity premium form.

target_gap: Give the receipt viewer an error/empty/loading state so a failed load isn't a silent blank.
evidence: Receipt viewer branches on viewingReceipt.endsWith('.pdf') to choose iframe vs . uploadExpenseReceipt names files `${team}/${id}_${Date.now()}.${ext}` so the public URL DOES end in the ext — but there is no error/onError fallback on the or
recommendation: Add onError fallback (e.g. 'Couldn't load receipt — open in new tab') and a loading state; consider matching by stored mime rather than URL suffix. (Moot until the upload path is wired per the critical finding, but required once it is.)

sub_feature: Expense form (live path) — uses legacy Drawer, not Fairway ModalShell/Sheet
target_gap: Unify the two coach-editor overlays under the Fairway overlay system for consistency.
evidence: The itinerary create/edit modal uses Fairway ModalShell (Radix Dialog), but the expense add/edit form on the SAME live page uses the legacy vaul Drawer (ExpenseForm.tsx:217-223). Two different overlay paradigms (centered Radix dialog vs bottom-sheet vaul) for the same role (coach add/edit) on one screen breaks Nielsen #4 Consistency & standards.
recommendation: Mount ExpenseForm inside a Fairway Sheet/ModalShell (the overlays already exist) or re-build it as a Fairway form so both editors share one overlay paradigm and token set.

target_gap: State the delete cascade (trip + expenses) before firing; two-tap with no consequence copy under-warns for a destructive cascade.
evidence: Delete is a two-tap inline confirm whose ONLY explanation is the button text 'Tap to confirm'; onBlur cancels it (176). It deletes the entire itinerary AND all its expenses (per the legacy copy 'All trip details and expenses will be removed') but the Fairway path gives no warning of the cascade and no modal — vs the itinerary delete in the legacy fork which DID show a full warning dialog. For a destructive cascade this is thin (Nielsen #5 error prevention).
recommendation: Either keep two-tap but add a tooltip/inline line naming the cascade ('Deletes the trip and its N expenses'), or use a ModalShell confirm consistent with the expense ConfirmDialog. Destructive cascades deserve an explicit consequence statement.

sub_feature: Detail panel header — coach edit/delete buttons on mobile
target_gap: Verify/raise the icon-only mobile tap targets to 44px; labels/aria are already correct.
evidence: Below sm the button labels are hidden (span hidden sm:inline) and the icons are aria-hidden, so the buttons rely SOLELY on aria-label (which is present here — good). The code comment itself flags this exact hazard. Acceptable because aria-label is set, but the icon-only 44px tap target is borderline (size='sm').
recommendation: Confirm size='sm' icon-only buttons meet the 44x44 touch target on mobile (WCAG 2.2 target size); if not, bump to size='md' on phones. aria-labels are correctly present, so this is target-size only.

target_gap: Route the no-team edge case through the Fairway EmptyState + add a next-action CTA.
evidence: The 'No Team Found' fallback renders OUTSIDE the Fairway shell with legacy classes (text-warm-900, text-warm-600) on a bare div, not the Fairway EmptyState/canvas used by the rest of the flag-on path. It's an unstyled-looking dead end with no CTA (e.g. 'Join a team').
recommendation: Render this through the Fairway EmptyState within the fairwayScope canvas and give it an action (link to join/roster). Keep the redesign path visually consistent even in the no-team edge case.

target_gap: Guarantee the CSV export isn't truncated by the 1000-row cap.
evidence: exportExpensesToCSV selects expenses with no .limit, so PostgREST's 1000-row default cap applies — an itinerary with >1000 expense rows would export a silently-truncated CSV. Unlikely per trip, but the export claims completeness.
recommendation: Add explicit .limit or paginate (fetchAllRowsResult pattern used elsewhere) so the export can never silently truncate; or document the cap. Low likelihood per-itinerary but it's a correctness guarantee.

sub_feature: Selection workspace — Coach pick Remove button
target_gap: Layer 3 requires confirmation/undo on destructive acts (Nielsen #5 error prevention + #3 user control). Add a confirm step or undo affordance.
evidence: <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => handleRemove(c.player_id)} busy={isPending} ...>Remove</Button> — handleRemove() calls removeQualifierCoachPick immediately with no confirm dialog and no undo; it permanently deletes a coach pick (player + reasoning) on a single click.
recommendation: Gate the destructive removal behind a confirmation (Fairway AlertDialog / overlay) or provide an undo toast (sonner action) that re-invokes setQualifierCoachPick with the prior reasoning. Restore the saved reasoning if the coach changes their mind.

sub_feature: Create qualifier — entry deadline date validation
target_gap: Layer 3 requires constraints + sensible defaults preventing invalid input (Nielsen #5). Cross-validate the three dates.
evidence: Entry-deadline input uses only min={today}; there is no constraint that entryDeadline <= startDate, and handleSubmit (lines 86-124) only validates name + startDate. A coach can set an entry deadline that falls AFTER the qualifier has already started, which is nonsensical and is accepted by createGolfQualifier (golf.ts golfQualifierSchema does not cross-check entryDeadline vs startDate either).
recommendation: Add a client check (and a Zod .refine in golfQualifierSchema) that entryDeadline <= startDate and endDate >= startDate; surface the error inline on the offending FormField rather than a single top error.

sub_feature: Loading state — route skeleton material mismatch
target_gap: Layer 3 requires a real loading skeleton that matches the actual content (states hard-gate). Re-skin the route skeletons onto Fairway tokens.
evidence: <div className="border-b border-warm-200/60 bg-cream-100/60 backdrop-blur-sm"> and surface-matte cards use legacy warm-* glass tokens. Next.js loading.tsx is route-level and flag-agnostic, so this skeleton renders for the Fairway path too — the load→content transition jumps from cream/glass chrome to bg-canvas matte Fairway surfaces.
recommendation: Replace the qualifiers loading.tsx with a Fairway-token skeleton (bg-canvas, Surface/Skeleton primitives, ViewHeader-shaped header) so the loading material matches the rendered page. Same fix needed for the workspace loading.tsx.

sub_feature: Selection workspace — loading skeleton uses glass tokens
target_gap: Layer 3 requires a content-matching skeleton. Rebuild on Fairway tokens.
evidence: <div className="h-24 bg-white/40 rounded-2xl animate-pulse mb-6" /> ... bg-white/40 blocks — arbitrary bg-white at 40% glass, not a Fairway surface skeleton; mismatches the FairwayQualifyingWorkspace it precedes.
recommendation: Use the Fairway Skeleton primitive on bg-canvas with Surface-shaped blocks mirroring the StateBar + Leaderboard + Coach-picks layout.

target_gap: Layer 3 requires every state designed with a next action (Nielsen #1/#10). Add an explicit not-entered/closed affordance for players.
evidence: primaryAction is null for a player who is NOT entered (canPlayRound is false), and the else branch only fires for isCoach. A non-entered player therefore sees a masthead with NO action and NO status telling them they aren't in this qualifier — they just see a leaderboard they can't join. There is no 'You're not entered in this qualifier' notice or request-to-enter affordance.
recommendation: When isPlayer && !canPlayRound, render an InlineNotice / quiet meta line clarifying state ('You're not entered' vs 'Entries closed' vs 'Qualifier completed'), and if a self-entry flow exists, surface it; otherwise tell the player to contact their coach.

sub_feature: List page — hero selects latest-start, not nearest-upcoming
target_gap: Layer 3 requires the focal element to be the truly most-relevant one. Re-derive hero by nearest/active rather than array head.
evidence: const hero = active[0] ?? null; — active is derived from a list ordered start_date DESC (page.tsx:52 .order('start_date', { ascending: false })). So among upcoming qualifiers the 'focal' hero is the one starting FURTHEST in the future, not the next one to play. An in_progress qualifier may also sort below a far-future upcoming one.
recommendation: Pick the hero by relevance: prefer an in_progress qualifier, else the upcoming with the SOONEST start_date (min future start). Sort the active bucket ascending by start_date for the hero choice while keeping the concluded list desc.

sub_feature: List page — no search / filter / sort / pagination
target_gap: Layer 3 requires search/filter where useful + handling 10x data. Add filter + bounded rendering.
evidence: Query .select('*').eq('team_id', teamId).order('start_date', desc) with NO .limit and NO pagination; FairwayQualifiers renders every concluded qualifier in a flat grid with no search/filter/status-tab. Over multiple seasons the Concluded section becomes an unbounded wall with no way to find a specific qualifier.
recommendation: Add a status segmented filter (Active/Concluded/All) and a name search in the ViewHeader; cap/paginate the concluded list (or lazy 'show more') to respect the PostgREST 1000-row ceiling and keep the page scannable.

sub_feature: Selection workspace — leaderboard not horizontally scrollable on mobile
target_gap: Layer 3 requires mobile parity / no horizontal squeeze. Add responsive scroll or stacked layout.
evidence: The SlotLeaderboard <ul> rows use fixed columns (w-7, w-12, w-14, w-28) + gap-4 with the name as flex-1, and there is NO overflow-x wrapper (unlike the detail-page tables which wrap in overflow-x-auto). ~244px of fixed columns + ~64px gaps leaves almost no room for the player name on a 320px phone, squeezing/wrapping the name.
recommendation: Wrap the list in an overflow-x-auto container with a min-width, or collapse the fixed columns into a stacked two-line row on small screens so the name + score stay legible.

sub_feature: Create qualifier — coach-pick max not recomputed when squad cleared
target_gap: Layer 3 requires constraints reflect actual state. Tie picks max to the real entered squad value.
evidence: Coach's-picks NumberField uses max={total}, but total is the fallback-coerced value (const total = slotsTotal && slotsTotal > 0 ? slotsTotal : 5). If the coach clears Squad size (slotsTotal=null), the picks field still allows up to 5 even though the visible squad size is empty/invalid, and the live read-out silently uses 5.
recommendation: Either disable/validate the picks field while squad size is empty, or visibly reflect that the squad defaults to 5; don't let the submitted picks exceed an unset squad value silently.

sub_feature: Leaderboard data fetch — unbounded rounds query (PostgREST cap)
target_gap: Layer 3 requires pagination past 1000 rows. Bound or paginate the rounds fetch.
evidence: supabase.from('golf_rounds').select(...).eq('qualifier_id', qualifierId) with no .limit/pagination. Per-qualifier round counts are small today, but the query relies on the default PostgREST 1000-row ceiling; a large multi-round qualifier with many entrants could silently truncate aggregates.
recommendation: Either add an explicit bound + assertion that count < 1000, or paginate via fetchAllRowsResult (the established helper) to guarantee complete per-player aggregates.

target_gap: Polish: make the empty-state number unambiguous; already near Layer 3.
evidence: EmptyState description=`All entries are within the top-${candidates.length - eligible.length} auto-lock…` — when eligible.length===0, candidates.length - eligible.length equals candidates.length, so it reads 'within the top-N auto-lock' where N is the full candidate count rather than the configured topScoreSlots. The number shown is the count of locked players, which is correct, but the phrasing 'top-N auto-lock' conflates lock-count with the configured top-score slot count and can mislead when
recommendation: Use topScoreSlots (the configured number) in the copy, or rephrase to 'Every entry is auto-locked — no discretionary picks needed' to avoid an ambiguous derived number.

sub_feature: List page — qualifier card 'View leaderboard' label vs upcoming state
target_gap: Polish: status-aware microcopy (Nielsen #2). Already near Layer 3.
evidence: Both the hero and every card render the CTA 'View leaderboard' regardless of status. For an 'Upcoming' qualifier with zero rounds there is no leaderboard yet (the detail shows an 'Awaiting first round' empty state), so the label over-promises.
recommendation: Vary the CTA by status: 'View details' for upcoming, 'View leaderboard' for in_progress, 'View results' for completed — matching what the detail page will actually show.

sub_feature: Detail page — selection cut-lines/tier badges shown to players
target_gap: Polish/permission-intent: make player-visibility of provisional selections an explicit, intentional choice.
evidence: FairwayQualifierLeaderboard is rendered for ALL viewers (no isCoach gate) and is passed selectionSlotsTotal/coachPick, so it draws 'In lineup'/'Bubble'/'Travel cut'/'Top-score line' to players in real time. This may be intended transparency, but exposing provisional bubble/cut status to players mid-qualifier is a coaching-sensitivity decision that isn't gated or documented.
recommendation: Confirm with product whether provisional lineup tiers should be player-visible; if not, gate the cut-line/tier rendering behind isCoach (the component already accepts the data, just gate the draw).

target_gap: Every implied sub-feature must have a real control; an entire CRUD verb (delete) is missing from the UI while existing in the backend.
evidence: TeeRow only renders an 'Edit' button (<Button ... onClick={onEdit}>Edit</Button>); there is no delete/remove control for a tee, and the drawer has no 'Delete course' action. Meanwhile softDeleteCourse/restoreCourse (course-library.ts:608-613) and softDeleteTee/restoreTee (course-library.ts:978-983) are fully implemented + unit-tested but have zero callers in any .tsx (confirmed by grep — only the test file references them).
recommendation: Add a destructive 'Delete tee set' action on each TeeRow (overflow menu or trailing icon) wired to softDeleteTee, and a 'Remove course' action in the detail drawer's action row wired to softDeleteCourse, both behind a confirmation. Surface restore for soft-deleted items (or document them as admin-only and remove the dead public actions).

target_gap: A status the UI displays (pinned/default tee) must be controllable; displaying a state with no way to change it is a dead affordance.
evidence: The 'Pinned' badge is render-only ({pinned && ...Pinned}); pinned comes from saved.pinned but nothing in the UI calls setTeamCoursePinned (course-library.ts:1091). A coach can SEE a pin state but can never set or clear it. Same for setTeamCourseDefaultTee (course-library.ts:1072) — playedMeta() shows 'Default: ' but there is no control to choose/change the default tee.
recommendation: Add a pin/unpin toggle (e.g. in the detail drawer action row for coaches) calling setTeamCoursePinned, and a 'Set as team default' affordance on each TeeRow calling setTeamCourseDefaultTee, with optimistic UI + toast.

target_gap: A premium catalog never shows the same item twice in one view; dedupe the shelves so each course appears once.
evidence: heroCourse = heroSaved?.course ?? courses[0]; then 'All courses' does courses.map(...) over the full list which still includes courses[0]. The hero card and the first 'All courses' card are the SAME course. Likewise 'Your team's courses' (savedRest) renders courses that ALSO appear in the 'All courses' grid below — the same course renders twice on one screen.
recommendation: Exclude the hero course id and the saved-course ids from the 'All courses' grid (filter them out), or relabel 'All courses' as 'More courses' and dedupe against what's already shown above.

target_gap: A link control must produce a working link for the most common input; require/normalize the scheme.
evidence: website is persisted as nullable(form.website) — only trimmed, never scheme-normalized. CourseDetailDrawer.tsx:207-214 renders <a href={course.website} target="_blank">. A coach who types 'pinehurst.com' (the natural input) stores 'pinehurst.com'; the anchor href is then a RELATIVE link that navigates to /golf/dashboard/pinehurst.com (broken). type="url" does not force a scheme.
recommendation: Normalize on save: if the value has no scheme, prepend 'https://' (and reject obviously invalid input). Optionally guard the render: only link if the stored value parses as http/https via new URL().

target_gap: Every data surface needs a real error state with retry that is visually distinct from empty; a cheerful empty masking a failure is an explicit B3 fail.
evidence: listCourses/getCourseTeeCounts/getTeamSavedCourses all swallow errors and return [] / {} (e.g. course-library.ts:147-149 'if (error || !data) return []'). The page then renders <EmptyState> ('No courses yet ... Add your first course') which is identical whether the library is genuinely empty or the query FAILED. There is no list-level error+retry state — the route error boundary only catches thrown errors, and these reads never throw.
recommendation: Have the reads distinguish failure from empty (return a discriminated result or throw on hard error so error.tsx engages), and render a distinct 'Couldn't load courses — Retry' state instead of the cheerful empty state masking a failure (hard-gate B3).

target_gap: Consistency & standards (Nielsen #4) and one-token-system discipline (C2): the live path must use a single button component, not a legacy fork.
evidence: import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button' — the LEGACY button (ui/button.tsx variants use bg-white, text-warm-700, bg-warm-50, text-red-600, ripple span, and 'hover:-translate-y-0.5' with NO motion-reduce guard). The rest of the live Fairway path imports '@/components/fairway/controls/button' (e.g. FairwayCoursePicker.tsx:42). All four course drawers (CourseDetailDrawer, CourseFormDrawer, TeeFormDrawer) inherit this legacy button, so /courses visually diverges (different radius/shadow/moti
recommendation: Swap to @/components/fairway/controls/button across CourseLibraryClient + the four drawers so the live path uses one button language; add motion-reduce to any retained translate-y hover.

target_gap: Confirmations on destructive acts (E / Nielsen #5) and undo where applicable.
evidence: handleRemoveImage immediately calls removeCourseImage on a single tap of the trash button (no window.confirm, no AlertDialog) — grep for 'confirm' in courses/ returns nothing. Removing a coach-uploaded course photo is destructive and instant; the only recovery is re-uploading.
recommendation: Gate 'Remove photo' behind a confirmation (AlertDialog) or provide an undo toast (Nielsen #5 error prevention / #3 user control).

target_gap: Search must work across the full dataset (data: handles 10x rows) and offer clear/efficiency shortcuts (Nielsen #7).
evidence: The search <input type="search"> has no clear ('x') button beyond the native one (inconsistent across browsers/iOS), no debounce, and no keyboard shortcut. Filtering is purely client-side over the 200-row page load — a library that grows past the listCourses limit (200, course-library.ts:123) silently can't be searched for entries beyond row 200. The page never calls listCourses with opts.query, so the server-side searchable path is unused.
recommendation: Either keep client filtering but raise/scroll the cap and add a visible clear button + debounce, or switch to server-side search (listCourses({ query })) so results aren't bounded by the first-page slice. Add a ⌘K / '/' focus shortcut for the frequent action.

target_gap: Surface the existing provenance data; either wire it or drop the orphaned read.
evidence: getCourseEditHistory is implemented (append-only golf_course_edit_history / golf_course_tee_edit_history are written on every create/update/delete) but never surfaced — no component imports it. 'Last edited <date>' (CourseDetailDrawer.tsx:253-257) is the only provenance shown; the rich who-changed-what history is invisible.
recommendation: Add a collapsible 'History' section or a small 'Edited by N people' affordance in the detail drawer that opens the edit-history list (a premium 'community-edited' trust signal). Or remove the unused action.

target_gap: Numbers must be honest in context; a partial sum shown as a course par is a soft data-lie.
evidence: TeeRow shows 'Par {total_par}' and '{total_yards} yds' even for is_draft tees whose hole set is incomplete. total_par/total_yards are summed only over the rows that exist (course-library.ts sumPar/sumYards), so a draft 9-of-18 tee can display a misleadingly small 'Par 27' next to a 'Draft' chip without clarifying the figure is partial.
recommendation: When is_draft, suppress or qualify the total ('Par 27 of 18 holes' / 'partial') so the number is never read as a complete-course par.

sub_feature: Detail drawer — tee section uses ad-hoc skeleton; full-detail load has no error path
target_gap: All three states (incl. error+retry) designed on every data surface, including the drawer detail fetch.
evidence: getCourseDetail(courseId).then(setDetail).finally(...) has no .catch — if the fetch rejects, loading clears, detail stays null, and the hero shows 'Loading…' (CourseDetailDrawer.tsx:171) forever with no error/retry. The tee skeleton (lines 232-237) uses raw animate-pulse divs rather than the Fairway Skeleton primitive used in loading.tsx, a minor inconsistency.
recommendation: Add a .catch that sets an error state with a retry button inside the drawer; reuse the Fairway <Skeleton> primitive for the tee loading rows for visual consistency.

sub_feature: Pin / default-tee — no empty-state guidance for coach
target_gap: Make the team-library capability discoverable without first drilling into a course.
evidence: 'Your team's courses' only renders when savedRest.length > 0; a coach with zero saved courses sees no section and no hint that 'Save to team' (only reachable inside the detail drawer, CourseDetailDrawer.tsx:185-193) exists. The team-library feature is discoverable only after opening a course.
recommendation: Show a quiet coach-only prompt in the header or an empty 'Team courses' rail ('Save courses your team plays for one-tap access') so the team-library capability is visible up front (Nielsen #6 recognition over recall).

target_gap: A real backend failure must render the error surface (explain + retry), never the 'More rounds needed' empty. Add an explicit retry button calling loadAll(playerId).
evidence: setLoadError only fires when detailedRes/trendRes/standingRes/leakRes are ALL status==='rejected'. But getDetailedStats (stats-data.ts:1059-1062) and getTrendAnalysis (stats-data.ts:~1530 catch -> return emptyResponse) swallow every error and RESOLVE with empty data; getPlayerStandingRows/getPlayerLeakMaps (stats-leak-maps.ts:539-544, 572-577) catch and RESOLVE with {success:false}. None ever reject, so loadError is dead code.
recommendation: Make the loaders signal failure distinctly from emptiness (e.g. getDetailedStats returns {ok:false} on caught error, or the leak/standing {success:false,error} is treated as an error not an empty). In loadAll, set loadError when any PRIMARY fetch reports a real failure (not just rejection), and gate isColdStart so it only renders when fetches succeeded with zero data.

target_gap: Every empty state needs a helpful next action (hard-gate B2 / Definition-of-Done STATES empty+CTA).
evidence: <EmptyState title="More rounds needed" description="Log 5+ rounds..."/> is rendered with NO `action` prop. EmptyState supports a primary CTA slot (EmptyState.tsx:46,115-120) but none is passed, so the empty state has no next action.
recommendation: Pass action={<Link href="/golf/dashboard/rounds/new">Log a round</Link>} (player view) so the empty state drives the obvious next step, matching the 'no player selected' empty which DOES have a CTA.

target_gap: Loading skeleton must match the real content's tokens, width and shape — no jarring two-stage flash or CLS.
evidence: loading.tsx returns <DetailedStatsSkeleton/>, which is the LEGACY skeleton (skeleton.tsx:1327+): bg-warm-200/cream-100/surface-matte tokens, max-w-4xl (896px), category-pills layout. The live Fairway cockpit uses max-w-[1200px], a tabbed layout, and an InstrumentPanel hero — so the route skeleton mismatches the real content in both design language and width, producing a two-stage flash (legacy skeleton -> cockpit StatsLoading -> content) with a layout shift.
recommendation: Replace the route loading.tsx with a Fairway-scoped skeleton mirroring the cockpit's own StatsLoading (FairwayStatsCockpit.tsx:2309) at max-w-[1200px] inside .fairway-ds, or render <StatsLoading/> directly so the loading shape matches.

target_gap: Premium KPI band shows movement (delta/trend), not just a static current value.
evidence: The 'fundamentals' row (Rounds/Fairways/GIR/Putts) renders Readouts with value + label only — no delta or trend, even though period comparison data exists (trendData.periodComparison 30d vs prev) and is computed. The deltas are instead buried in the collapsed 'Full shot detail' disclosure (lines 1947-1979).
recommendation: Surface a delta line on each vitals Readout (Readout supports a `delta` prop, Readout.tsx:102-103) using last-30d vs prev-30d, so the KPI row reads as a premium dashboard KPI band (label + value + delta + trend) per criteria C3.

target_gap: A stats sheet a coach/player would want to share or print needs an export affordance.
evidence: The Fairway stats surface has no export/print/share affordance. The legacy stats path shipped src/components/golf/stats/exportPdf.ts (PDF export); the redesign dropped it. A coach viewing a player's full stat sheet has no way to export or share it.
recommendation: Add an Export / Print action (PDF or print stylesheet) to the masthead actions slot, reusing or porting exportPdf.ts. Stats sheets are a high-value export surface (criteria E DATA: export where useful).

sub_feature: Filter chips (scrambling cut / approach lie / putt break)
target_gap: Touch targets >=44px on mobile (Definition-of-Done RESPONSIVE).
evidence: ToggleChip is sized 'min-h-9 ... py-1.5' (36px tall). WCAG 2.2 / premium touch-target bar wants >=44px. These are primary in-tab filters tapped frequently on mobile.
recommendation: Bump ToggleChip to min-h-11 (44px) or add adequate vertical padding so the tap target meets 44px.

target_gap: Mutually-exclusive filters should expose group/single-select semantics to AT.
evidence: Each toggle group is a <div aria-label="...filter"> containing individual <button aria-pressed> chips. A labeled div is not a grouping role, so assistive tech does not announce the set as a single-select group; aria-pressed toggle buttons (vs radios) also don't convey 'one of N'.
recommendation: Wrap each chip set in role="group" (keep aria-label) or model them as a radiogroup (role=radiogroup + role=radio/aria-checked) since they are mutually exclusive single-selects.

target_gap: Secondary surfaces must also not mask failures as empties.
evidence: When getPlayerLeakMaps returns {success:false} (auth/backend error), leakMaps stays null and the Approach/Putting tabs pass data=[] to LeakMap, which derives state 'insufficient-data' (LeakMap.tsx:120-122). A backend failure therefore reads as 'not enough data' inside an otherwise-populated page — a second instance of failure-masked-as-empty (same root cause as the primary finding, but on a secondary enrichment).
recommendation: Distinguish leak-fetch failure from genuine no-data and render an inline 'Couldn't load leak maps — retry' notice in that band rather than the insufficient-data state.

target_gap: Reach Layer 4: remember/restore the user's selected tab; allow deep-linking to a tab.
evidence: <Tabs defaultValue="scoring"> is uncontrolled with no URL/localStorage sync. Navigating to a round and back, refreshing, or deep-linking always resets to Scoring; selected tab is not shareable or remembered.
recommendation: Sync the active tab to a ?tab= search param (or localStorage) so refresh/back/deep-link preserves the user's place — a Layer-4 'remembers prefs' delight that is cheap here.

target_gap: Token-only typography (no arbitrary px sizes).
evidence: TabsTrigger uses arbitrary 'text-[13px]' rather than a design-token type size (e.g. text-label / text-body-sm). C2 requires design-tokens only, no text-[NNpx] arbitrary literals.
recommendation: Replace text-[13px] with the nearest Fairway type token to keep the type scale token-disciplined.

target_gap: Coach single-player view should name the player it is showing.
evidence: Coach with no ?player= is redirected to /stats/team; a coach viewing ?player= gets title 'Player stats' with no player name (playerName='' because isCoachView short-circuits name to '') and a generic back link. The cockpit body is shared but the masthead never shows WHICH player the coach is viewing on this route (only the roster/[id] wrapper supplies identity).
recommendation: For the coach ?player= case, resolve and show the player's name in the title (fetch from the standing/detailed payload) so 'whose stats' is never ambiguous (Nielsen #2/#6 recognition).

target_gap: Surface the error state on optimistic-write failure (toast/inline) so the silent revert is explained — required for gate B3 (designed error state) and Nielsen #1/#9.
evidence: handleCompleteTask: on failure it only `setTasks(... revert ...)` then `router.refresh()`. There is NO fairwayToast.error / no user feedback. TaskRow (hub-parts.tsx:403-411) also only try/finally with no error surface. The optimistic check flips back with zero explanation.
recommendation: On `!result.success`, after reverting, call fairwayToast.error(result.error || 'Could not mark task complete. Please try again.'). Mirror the legacy hub's optimistic-set + toast + badge-refetch contract referenced in the wrapper's own docblock.

target_gap: Error prevention on the destructive-edit path + dirty-state — required for gate B (error prevention) and data integrity.
evidence: The edit form Save button has only `busy={isPending}` — no `disabled={!teamName.trim()}` (unlike the create form at line 250). handleUpdateTeam (line 152-169) sends `name: teamName.trim()` unconditionally, and updateTeam (teams.ts:435) writes `updateData.name = updates.name.trim()` with no min-length check. A coach can clear the name and Save → empty team name persisted.
recommendation: Add `disabled={!teamName.trim()}` to the Save button AND a guard in handleUpdateTeam (toast 'Team name is required'). Defensively, reject empty trimmed names in updateTeam server action. Also disable Save when nothing changed (name===team.name && season===team.season) for a real dirty-state.

target_gap: Skeleton must match the live Fairway design system + page shape (gate B3, no jarring token/shape swap).
evidence: `export default function Loading() { return <GenericPageSkeleton />; }` and GenericPageSkeleton (skeleton.tsx:1579-1613) renders legacy chrome: `surface-matte rounded-3xl`, `bg-warm-200/60`, `bg-cream-100/75`, `rounded-xl` — none of the Fairway `--fw-*` tokens. Under the redesign flag the user sees a legacy-styled skeleton then a Fairway page.
recommendation: Replace with a Fairway-native skeleton (Skeleton/SkeletonCard from @/components/fairway/feedback) wrapped in fairwayScope('min-h-full bg-canvas'), shape-matched to the masthead + form sections — exactly as team-hub/loading.tsx already does.

target_gap: A dedicated, retry-capable error state for the route (gate B3).
evidence: The team-hub directory has only page.tsx + loading.tsx (verified via ls); no error.tsx. The page fires 6 parallel Supabase queries (Promise.all) with no try/catch; a throw bubbles to the distant parent (dashboard)/error.tsx, losing the team-hub-specific recovery copy that /team has via its own error.tsx.
recommendation: Add src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/team-hub/error.tsx using RouteErrorBoundary (mirror team/error.tsx) with title 'Failed to load Team Hub' + retry, so a query failure shows a designed error+retry rather than a generic boundary.

target_gap: Gender selectable on first-team creation so the stored gender is correct (gate B4 no data lies, completeness).
evidence: handleCreateTeam calls `createTeam(teamName, season)` with no gender arg; createTeam (teams.ts:304-308) signature is `gender: 'mens'|'womens' = 'mens'`. The no-team create form (lines 208-258) has only name + season fields — no gender picker — even though the add-second-team panel does (lines 451-466). A women's-program head creating their first team here silently gets a men's team.
recommendation: Add the same Men's/Women's gender picker to the create-first-team FormSection and pass it to createTeam(teamName, season, gender). The data lie (wrong gender) propagates to team theming and the men/women toggle.

target_gap: Every shipped surface must be reachable from persistent nav and not duplicate a sibling (gate B2/B1, Nielsen #4).
evidence: The player nav rail 'Team' group lists only My Qualifiers, Roster, and Team Hub — there is NO entry for /golf/dashboard/team. The player FairwayTeamInfo surface is reachable only by direct URL / the legacy CommandPalette ('Team Info' → /golf/dashboard/team, CommandPalette.tsx:105). src/TODO.md:66 self-flags '/golf/dashboard/team is not linked from anywhere.'
recommendation: Either remove the player FairwayTeamInfo surface (its content — coach, announcements, tasks, roster — fully overlaps Team Hub) or give it a rail entry. As-is it is an orphaned, duplicate page a player can't reliably reach.

sub_feature: Player Team Info vs Team Hub — redundancy
target_gap: Single coherent player team surface (Nielsen #4 consistency, #8 minimalism).
evidence: FairwayTeamInfo shows Head coach, Announcements (slice 3), My tasks, Team roster (slice 5), Team info. FairwayTeamHub (FairwayTeamHub.tsx:164-255) shows Tasks, Announcements, Travel, Classes, Teammates. target_gap: Paginate past the PostgREST 1000-row cap (or aggregate server-side) so roster card stats stay correct as a team accumulates seasons of rounds.
evidence: const { data: allRounds } = await supabase.from('golf_rounds').select('player_id, total_score, holes_played').in('player_id', playerIds).not('total_score', 'is', null);  // NO .order().range() — and no season/date bound at all (ALL rounds ever)

As written it silently truncates at 1000 rows, so a team whose combined round history exceeds 1000 shows under-counted rounds_count and a skewed avg_score on every roster card.

sub_feature: Team Stats — team rounds aggregate (averages, rankings, teamRoundIds)
target_gap: Paginate the team rounds query so team averages/rankings/scrambling are correct at full-season scale, matching the paginated holes query it feeds.
evidence: const { data: roundsData } = await supabase.from('golf_rounds').select('id, player_id, total_score, ...').in('player_id', playerIds).eq('status','completed').not('total_score','is',null).gte('round_date', seasonStartDate);  // 12-month bound but NO pagination; const teamRoundIds = roundsData.map(r=>r.id) then feeds a paginated holes query

sub_feature: Messages — conversations rail unread count / last message
target_gap: Move unread/last-message aggregation server-side so the rail is correct and cheap on high-volume team chats (10x messages).
evidence: const { data: allOtherMessages } = await supabase.from('golf_messages').select('conversation_id, created_at').in('conversation_id', teamChatIds).neq('sender_id', userId);  // also line 483: full golf_messages fetch ordered desc with no .limit, then unread computed client-side by counting rows
recommendation: Compute unread counts and last-message in SQL (a head/count query per the unread predicate, or fold into get_golf_conversations_with_details). Fetching every message of every team chat to count them client-side transfers up to the PostgREST 1000-row cap per call and UNDER-counts unread once a team chat exceeds 1000 messages — a busy team's badge silently caps/goes wrong.

sub_feature: Team Category Insights — recent-rounds trend window
target_gap: Distribute the round window per-player so every player gets their last ~10 rounds for the trend calc, regardless of how active teammates are.
evidence: .from('golf_rounds').select(ROUND_STAT_COLUMNS.join(', ')).in('player_id', playerIds).eq('status','completed').order('round_date',{ascending:false}).limit(playerIds.length * 10) // 'Up to 10 rounds per player' — but the cap is GLOBAL, not per-player
recommendation: Fetch the most-recent N rounds PER player (a lateral/DISTINCT-ON RPC, or per-player capped queries), not a single global limit. A global .limit(playerIds.length*10) ordered by round_date lets the most-active players consume all slots, so the trend (recentSlice/previousSlice at line 766) is computed from zero rounds for less-active players — under-reporting trends precisely for the players a coach most needs flagged.

sub_feature: Client bundle size — eager heavy Fairway page components
